title.zh: 卷五十一 列傳第四十五 處士
title.raw: 卷五十一 列傳第四十五 處士 Volume 51: Retired Gentlemen

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「君子遁世無悶，獨立不懼。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The noble man withdraws from the world without vexation; he stands alone without fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "The noble man may leave the world yet feel no vexation; he may stand alone yet feel no fear.

sentences.zh: 」孔子稱長沮、桀溺隱者也。

translations.literal: " Confucius called Changju and Jieni recluses.
translations.idiomatic: " Confucius praised Changju and Jieni as men who had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 古之隱者，或恥聞禪代，高讓帝王，以萬乘爲垢辱，之死亡而無悔。

translations.literal: Recluses of old, shamed to hear of abdication and transfer of the throne, loftily yielded the imperial seat and took the chariot of ten thousand as filth and disgrace, going to death without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who withdrew, shamed by tales of abdication, refused the throne and treated imperial power as stain and shame, facing death without regret.

sentences.zh: 此則輕生重道，希世間出，隱之上者也。

translations.literal: These lightly valued life and heavily valued the Way, hoping to leave the common world—they are recluses of the highest kind.
translations.idiomatic: They prized the Way above life and sought to step outside the world—the highest sort of recluse.

sentences.zh: 或託仕監門，寄臣柱下，居易而以求其志，處汙而不愧其色。

translations.literal: Some took office as gatekeepers, others lodged as ministers beneath the pillar, dwelling in ease to seek their aim and standing in filth without shame on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Some served as gatekeepers or clerks under the pillar, living simply to pursue their purpose and dwelling in corruption without losing their color.

sentences.zh: 此所謂大隱隱於市朝，又其次也。

translations.literal: This is what is called great reclusion hidden in market and court—the next rank down.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great recluse who hides in market and court—the next rank.

sentences.zh: 或裸體佯狂，盲喑絕世，棄禮樂以反道，忍孝慈而不恤。

translations.literal: Some went naked and feigned madness, blind and mute, cutting themselves off from the age, casting aside rites and music to return to the Way, enduring the abandonment of filial piety and kindness without care.
translations.idiomatic: Some stripped naked and played mad, blind and mute, rejecting the age, casting off rites and music for the Way and enduring without filial kindness.

sentences.zh: 此全身遠害，得大雅之道，又其次也。

translations.literal: These preserved the body and kept far from harm, attaining the Way of the great Odes—the next rank down again.
translations.idiomatic: These kept body whole and harm distant, attaining the great Odes' Way—again the next rank.

sentences.zh: 然同不失語默之致，有幽人貞吉矣。

translations.literal: Yet alike they did not lose the reach of silence and speech; they had the reclusive man's steadfast good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all alike kept the balance of silence and speech and possessed the reclusive man's steadfast fortune.

sentences.zh: 與夫沒身亂世，爭利干時者，豈同年而語哉！

translations.literal: Compared with those who end their lives in a chaotic age and strive for profit against the times—can they be spoken of in the same year?
translations.idiomatic: How can they be named in the same breath as men who waste their lives in chaos and scramble for profit?

sentences.zh: 《孟子》曰：「今人之於爵祿，得之若其生，失之若其死。

translations.literal: Mencius says: "People today toward rank and stipend—gaining them is like gaining life, losing them is like losing life.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius says, "Today's men treat rank and salary as they do life itself—gain feels like birth, loss like death.

sentences.zh: 」《淮南子》曰：「人皆鑒於止水，不鑒於流潦。

translations.literal: " The Huainanzi says: "All men mirror themselves in still water, not in rushing flood.
translations.idiomatic: " The Huainanzi says, "Everyone takes his mirror from still water, never from a rushing torrent.

sentences.zh: 」夫可以揚清激濁，抑貪止競，其惟隱者乎！

translations.literal: " Who can clarify the muddy, stir the pure, check greed and halt rivalry? Only the recluse!
translations.idiomatic: " Who can clarify what is foul, lift what is pure, and curb greed and rivalry? Only the recluse.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王，莫不崇尚其道。

translations.literal: From antiquity no emperor or king has failed to honor this Way.
translations.idiomatic: Every emperor and king since antiquity has honored this Way.

sentences.zh: 雖唐堯不屈巢、許，周武不降夷、齊；

translations.literal: Though Tang Yao did not bow to Chao and Xu, and King Wu of Zhou did not descend to Yi and Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yao would not bow to Chao and Xu, and King Wu would not humble himself before Yi and Qi;

sentences.zh: 以漢高肆慢而長揖黃、綺，光武按法而折意嚴、周；

translations.literal: Han Gaozu in his insolence yet received the long bow of Huang and Qi, and Guangwu applied the law yet bent his will before Yan and Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: yet Han Gaozu, for all his rudeness, met Huang and Qi with a long bow, and Guangwu bent the law for Yan and Zhou;

sentences.zh: 自茲以來，世有人矣！

translations.literal: from then on, generation after generation has had such men!
translations.idiomatic: and since then every age has known such men.

sentences.zh: 有梁之盛，繼紹風猷。

translations.literal: In the splendor of Liang they continued this wind and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Liang at its height carried on this tradition.

sentences.zh: 斯乃道德可宗，學藝可範，故以備《處士篇》云。

translations.literal: These were men whose virtue could be taken as model and whose learning and craft could be taken as pattern—hence they fill the "Biographies of Retired Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Their conduct could be honored and their arts imitated—hence this "Biographies of Retired Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 何點字子晳，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Dian, styled Zishe, was a man of Qian in Lujiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He Dian, styled Zishe, came from Qian in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖尚之，宋司空。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shangzhi was Song Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shangzhi had been Song Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 父鑠，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His father Shuo was Grand Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuo was grand administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 鑠素有風疾，無故害妻，坐法死。

translations.literal: Shuo had long suffered wind illness and without cause harmed his wife; by law he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo had long suffered a wind disorder and, without cause, killed his wife; he was executed by law.

sentences.zh: 點年十一，幾至滅性。

translations.literal: Dian at eleven nearly destroyed himself in grief.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Dian nearly destroyed himself in mourning.

sentences.zh: 及長，感家禍，欲絕婚宦，尚之強爲之娶琅邪王氏。

translations.literal: When grown, moved by the family calamity, he wished to renounce marriage and office; Shangzhi forced him to marry a woman of the Wang clan of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he wished to renounce marriage and office after the family tragedy; Shangzhi forced him to wed a woman of the Wang clan of Langya.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，將親迎，點累涕泣，求執本志，遂得罷。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete and he was to go fetch the bride in person, Dian wept again and again, begging to hold to his original resolve, and at last was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended and he was to fetch the bride, Dian wept and begged to keep his resolve until the wedding was called off.

sentences.zh: 容貌方雅，博通羣書，善談論。

translations.literal: His bearing was square and refined; he mastered many books and was skilled in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Square and refined in bearing, he mastered many books and excelled in talk.

sentences.zh: 家本甲族，親姻多貴仕。

translations.literal: His family was originally of the first great clans, with many noble kin by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His house was of the highest clans, with many noble connections.

sentences.zh: 點雖不入城府，而遨遊人世，不簪不帶，或駕柴車，躡草矰，恣心所適，致醉而歸，士大夫多慕從之，時人號爲「通隱」。

translations.literal: Though Dian did not enter the city offices, he wandered the human world without cap or belt, sometimes driving a brushwood cart and treading grass sandals, going wherever his heart wished and returning drunk; many scholar-officials admired and followed him, and men of the time called him the "Universal Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: Though he never entered the prefectural city, he roamed the world bareheaded, sometimes in a brushwood cart and grass sandals, wandering until drunk while scholars flocked to him—men called him the Universal Recluse.

sentences.zh: 兄求，亦隱居吳郡虎丘山。

translations.literal: His elder brother Qiu also lived in retirement on Tiger Hill in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Qiu also dwelt in seclusion on Tiger Hill in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 求卒，點菜食不飲酒，訖于三年，要帶減半。

translations.literal: When Qiu died, Dian ate vegetables and drank no wine until the three years were done; his sash and belt were half what they had been.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiu died, Dian ate only vegetables and drank no wine for three years, his sash and belt half their former width.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始末，徵太子洗馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Song's Taishi era he was summoned as Crown Prince's Household Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song Taishi he was summoned as crown prince's household steward.

sentences.zh: 齊初，累徵中書郎、太子中庶子，並不就。

translations.literal: Early in Qi he was repeatedly summoned as Palace Secretary and Crown Prince's Household Vice-Attendant; he never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qi he was repeatedly summoned as palace secretary and crown prince's household vice-attendant and always refused.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝𤅢、吳國張融、會稽孔稚珪爲莫逆友。

translations.literal: With Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, Zhang Rong of Wu, and Kong Zhigui of Kuaiji he was bosom friend.
translations.idiomatic: With Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, Zhang Rong of Wu, and Kong Zhigui of Kuaiji he was inseparable friend.

sentences.zh: 從弟遁，以東籬門園居之，稚珪爲築室焉。

translations.literal: His cousin Dun took the Eastern Hedge Gate garden as his dwelling; Zhigui built a house for him there.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Dun lived in the Eastern Hedge Gate garden; Zhigui built him a house there.

sentences.zh: 園內有卞忠貞塚，點植花卉於塚側，每飲必舉酒酹之。

translations.literal: Within the garden was the tomb of Bian the Loyal Martyr; Dian planted flowers beside the tomb and whenever he drank always raised a cup and poured a libation.
translations.idiomatic: In the garden lay the tomb of Bian the Loyal Martyr; Dian planted flowers beside it and never drank without pouring a libation.

sentences.zh: 初，褚淵、王儉爲宰相，點謂人曰：「我作《齊書贊》，云『淵旣世族，儉亦國華；

translations.literal: Earlier, Chu Yuan and Wang Jian were chancellors; Dian told someone: "I wrote in my 'Praise for the Qi Annals,' 'Yuan is already a great clan, Jian also a national flower;
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Yuan and Wang Jian were chancellors, Dian said, "In my Praise for the Qi Annals I wrote, 'Yuan is already a great clan, Jian also a national flower;

sentences.zh: 不賴舅氏，遑恤國家』。

translations.literal: not relying on maternal kin, how could they spare thought for the state.'
translations.idiomatic: not relying on maternal kin—how could they spare thought for the state?'

sentences.zh: 」王儉聞之，欲候點，知不可見，乃止。

translations.literal: " When Wang Jian heard this he wished to visit Dian but knew he could not be seen and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jian wished to visit when he heard this but knew Dian would not receive him and desisted.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷命駕造點，點從後門遁去。

translations.literal: Prince Jingling of Yuzhang ordered his carriage to visit Dian; Dian slipped out the back gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling of Yuzhang drove to visit him; Dian fled by the back gate.

sentences.zh: 司徒、竟陵王子良欲就見之，點時在法輪寺，子良乃往請，點角巾登席，子良欣悅無已，遺點嵇叔夜酒杯、徐景山酒鐺。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works, Prince Ziliang of Jingling, wished to go see him; Dian was then at Falun Temple, and Ziliang went to invite him; Dian came to the mat in a kerchief, and Ziliang was endlessly delighted and sent Dian Ji Kang's wine cup and Xu Jingshan's wine kettle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling wished to see him; Dian was at Falun Temple and Ziliang went to invite him; Dian took the mat in a kerchief while Ziliang rejoiced and sent Ji Kang's wine cup and Xu Jingshan's wine kettle.

sentences.zh: 點少時嘗患渴痢，積歲不愈。

translations.literal: In youth Dian once suffered from wasting thirst and dysentery and for years was not cured.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he suffered wasting thirst and dysentery for years without cure.

sentences.zh: 後在吳中石佛寺建講，於講所晝寢，夢一道人形貌非常，授丸一掬，夢中服之，自此而差，時人以爲淳德所感。

translations.literal: Later at Stone Buddha Monastery in Wu he established a lecture; at the lecture hall he napped by day and dreamed of a Taoist of extraordinary appearance who gave him a handful of pills; in the dream he swallowed them, and from then on he recovered—men of the time took it as the response of pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Stone Buddha Monastery in Wu he lectured; napping in the hall he dreamed a Taoist of strange aspect gave him a handful of pills; he swallowed them in the dream and recovered—men called it the reward of pure virtue.

sentences.zh: 性通脫，好施與，遠近致遺，一無所逆，隨復散焉。

translations.literal: By nature he was free and easy, fond of giving; gifts came from far and near and he refused none, soon scattering them again.
translations.idiomatic: Free and generous by nature, he accepted gifts from far and near and soon gave them all away again.

sentences.zh: 嘗行經朱雀門街，有自車後盜點衣者，見而不言，傍有人擒盜與之，點乃以衣施盜，盜不敢受，點命告有司，盜懼，乃受之，催令急去。

translations.literal: Once passing along Vermilion Bird Gate Street, someone stole clothing from behind his cart; he saw it but said nothing; a bystander seized the thief and returned the clothes; Dian then gave the clothes to the thief; the thief dared not accept; Dian ordered him reported to the authorities; the thief in fear then accepted and was urged to leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Once on Vermilion Bird Gate Street a man stole clothes from behind his cart; Dian saw but said nothing; when a bystander caught the thief and returned the clothes, Dian gave them to the thief; the thief refused until Dian threatened to report him, then fled in haste.

sentences.zh: 點雅有人倫識鑒，多所甄拔，知吳興丘遲於幼童，稱濟陽江淹於寒素，悉如其言。

translations.literal: Dian had fine discernment in human relations and promoted many; he knew Qiu Chi of Wu commandery as a child and praised Jiang Yan of Jiyang in humble circumstances—both exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: He judged men finely and advanced many; as a boy he marked Qiu Chi of Wu and Jiang Yan of Jiyang in poverty—both proved as he said.

sentences.zh: 點旣老，又娶魯國孔嗣女，嗣亦隱者也。

translations.literal: When Dian was old he again married the daughter of Kong Si of Lu; Si was also a recluse.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he again married the daughter of Kong Si of Lu, himself a recluse.

sentences.zh: 點雖婚，亦不與妻相見，築別室以處之，人莫喻其意也。

translations.literal: Though married, Dian still did not meet his wife face to face, building a separate room to lodge her—no one understood his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though married, he never met his wife face to face but lodged her in a separate room—no one fathomed why.

sentences.zh: 吳國張融少時免官，而爲詩有高尚之言，點答詩曰：「昔聞東都日，不在簡書前。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong of Wu in youth had been dismissed from office and wrote poetry with lofty words; Dian answered in verse: "Long ago I heard of the eastern capital's sun—not yet before the bamboo annals."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong of Wu, dismissed young, wrote lofty verse; Dian replied, "Long ago I heard of the eastern capital's sun—not yet before the bamboo annals."

sentences.zh: 」雖戲也，而融久病之。

translations.literal: Though in jest, Rong took the wound to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though jest, Rong brooded on the barb.

sentences.zh: 及點後婚，融始爲詩贈點曰：「惜哉何居士，薄暮遘荒婬。

translations.literal: When Dian later married, Rong first wrote a poem to gift Dian: "Alas, Master He—at dusk you meet debauched lewdness."
translations.idiomatic: When Dian married at last, Rong sent verse: "Alas, Master He—at dusk you meet debauched lewdness."

sentences.zh: 」點亦病之，而無以釋也。

translations.literal: Dian too was wounded but had no way to explain.
translations.idiomatic: Dian smarted too but could not answer.

sentences.zh: 高祖與點有舊，及踐阼，手詔曰：「昔因多暇，得訪逸軌，坐脩竹，臨清池，忘今語古，何其樂也。

translations.literal: Gaozu had old ties with Dian; when he took the throne he wrote by hand: "Long ago in much leisure I could visit your hidden track, sit among bamboo by a clear pool, forget present speech for ancient talk—what joy!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had known Dian; on taking the throne he wrote, "Long ago in leisure I visited your hidden path, sat in bamboo by a clear pool, forgot present for ancient talk—what joy!

sentences.zh: 暫別丘園，十有四載，人事艱阻，亦何可言。

translations.literal: For a time I left hill and garden—fourteen years; human affairs were hard and obstructed—what more can be said.
translations.idiomatic: I left your hill garden fourteen years; affairs were hard—what more can be said.

sentences.zh: 自應運在天，每思相見，密邇物色，勞甚山阿。

translations.literal: Since Heaven's mandate was mine I have often wished to meet; I searched for you in secret, laboring much on mountain slopes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Heaven's mandate fell to me I have longed to meet you and searched the mountains in secret with great labor.

sentences.zh: 嚴光排九重，踐九等，談天人，敘故舊，有所不臣，何傷於高？

translations.literal: Yan Guang brushed aside the ninefold gates, trod the nine ranks, spoke of Heaven and man and old friendship—what harm if he would not be subject?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Guang brushed past the nine gates, walked the nine ranks, spoke of Heaven and man and old ties—what harm in one who would not bow?

sentences.zh: 文先以皮弁謁子桓，伯況以縠綃見文叔，求之往策，不無前例。

translations.literal: Wen first visited Zihuan in skin cap; Bozhuang met Wenshu in silk gauze—seeking precedents in former ages, there are none without earlier examples.
translations.idiomatic: Wen first visited Zihuan in skin cap; Bozhuang met Wenshu in gauze silk—former ages offer precedents enough.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿鹿皮巾等。

translations.literal: Now I gift you a deer-skin kerchief and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send you a deer-skin kerchief and the like.

sentences.zh: 後數日，望能入也。

translations.literal: In a few days I hope you can enter."
translations.idiomatic: In a few days I hope you will come in."

sentences.zh: 」點以巾褐引入華林園，高祖甚悅，賦詩置酒，恩禮如舊。

translations.literal: Dian was led into Hualin Garden in cloth and coarse dress; Gaozu was very pleased, composed poetry and set out wine, favor and courtesy as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Dian entered Hualin Garden in kerchief and homespun; Gaozu rejoiced, set out verse and wine, and treated him with the old kindness.

sentences.zh: 仍下詔曰：「前徵士何點，高尚其道，志安容膝，脫落形骸，棲志窅冥。

translations.literal: An edict followed: "Former Recluse He Dian—lofty in his Way, his will content with a knee's breadth of room, casting off the bodily frame, nesting his aim in the deep dark.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Former recluse He Dian—lofty in the Way, content with a knee's breadth of room, casting off the body, nesting his aim in the deep dark.

sentences.zh: 朕日昃思治，尚想前哲；

translations.literal: I toil at sunset thinking on government and still look up to former sages;
translations.idiomatic: I toil at government till sunset and still look up to former sages;

sentences.zh: 況親得同時，而不與爲政。

translations.literal: how much more when I have obtained one of the same time and do not govern with him.
translations.idiomatic: how much more when I hold one of the same age and do not govern with him.

sentences.zh: 喉脣任切，必俟邦良，誠望惠然，屈居獻替。

translations.literal: Throat and lips have urgent duty and must await the state's good men; I truly hope you will come graciously and bend to counsel and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Throat and lips have urgent work and must await the state's good men; I truly hope you will come and bend to counsel.

sentences.zh: 可徵爲侍中。

translations.literal: He may be summoned as Palace Attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be summoned as palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 」辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 乃復詔曰：「徵士何點，居貞物表，縱心塵外，夷坦之風，率由自遠。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Recluse He Dian dwells in integrity beyond things, lets his heart roam outside the dust; the easy and level wind he leads comes from far by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "Recluse He Dian dwells in integrity beyond things and lets his heart roam outside the dust; the easy wind he leads comes from afar by nature.

sentences.zh: 往因素志，頗申宴言，眷彼子陵，情兼惟舊。

translations.literal: Formerly, following his constant aim, we spoke freely at banquet; I cherish Ziling in feeling as well as old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, following his constant aim, we spoke freely at banquet; I cherish Ziling in feeling and old friendship alike.

sentences.zh: 昔仲虞邁俗，受俸漢朝；

translations.literal: In former ages Zhongyu transcended the vulgar and received salary from the Han court;
translations.idiomatic: In former ages Zhongyu transcended the vulgar and took salary from Han;

sentences.zh: 安道逸志，不辭晉祿。

translations.literal: Andao in reclusive will did not decline Jin stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Andao in reclusive will did not decline Jin stipend.

sentences.zh: 此蓋前代盛軌，往賢所同。

translations.literal: This is the great track of former generations, what past worthies held in common.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great track of former generations, what past worthies shared.

sentences.zh: 可議加資給，並出在所，日費所須，太官別給。

translations.literal: Let additional stipend be discussed and granted, issued from the place of residence; daily expenses as needed shall be separately supplied by the Imperial Commissary.
translations.idiomatic: Let additional stipend be discussed and granted from his place of residence; daily needs shall be separately supplied by the Imperial Commissary.

sentences.zh: 旣人高曜卿，故事同垣下。」

translations.literal: Since your virtue shines high, the precedent is the same as below the palace wall."
translations.idiomatic: Since your virtue shines high, the precedent is the same as below the palace wall."

sentences.zh: 天監三年，卒，時年六十八。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year three he died, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「新除侍中何點，棲遲衡泌，白首不渝。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The newly appointed Palace Attendant He Dian lingered at his hermitage by the ford and did not change white-haired to the end.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The newly appointed palace attendant He Dian lingered at his ford-side hermitage and did not change to the end.

sentences.zh: 奄至殞喪，倍懷傷惻。

translations.literal: Suddenly he reached ruin and death; my grief redoubles.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he died; my grief redoubles.

sentences.zh: 可給第一品材一具，賻錢二萬、布五十匹。

translations.literal: Let there be given one set of first-rank funeral timber, condolence money twenty thousand, and fifty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Grant one set of first-rank funeral timber, twenty thousand in condolence money, and fifty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 喪事所須，內監經理。

translations.literal: What the funeral requires shall be managed by the inner directorate."
translations.idiomatic: Funeral needs shall be managed by the inner directorate."

sentences.zh: 」又敕點弟胤曰：「賢兄徵君，弱冠拂衣，華首一操。

translations.literal: He also charged Dian's younger brother Yin: "Your worthy elder brother the Recluse at a tender age brushed away his robes and held one course to hoary head.
translations.idiomatic: He also charged Yin, Dian's younger brother: "Your worthy brother the recluse at a tender age brushed away office and held one course to hoary head.

sentences.zh: 心遊物表，不滯近跡；

translations.literal: His heart wandered outside things and did not cling to near traces;
translations.idiomatic: His heart wandered outside things and did not cling to near traces;

sentences.zh: 脫落形骸，寄之遠理。

translations.literal: he cast off the bodily frame and lodged it in far principle.
translations.idiomatic: he cast off the body and lodged it in far principle.

sentences.zh: 性情勝致，遇興彌高；

translations.literal: His nature's winning reach rose higher when stirred;
translations.idiomatic: His nature's winning reach rose higher when stirred;

sentences.zh: 文會酒德，撫際逾遠。

translations.literal: in literary gatherings and wine virtue he touched the distance ever farther.
translations.idiomatic: in literary gatherings and wine virtue he touched ever farther distances.

sentences.zh: 朕膺籙受圖，思長聲教。

translations.literal: I received the mandate and took the chart, thinking to extend sound teaching long.
translations.idiomatic: I received the mandate and took the chart, thinking to extend sound teaching.

sentences.zh: 朝多君子，旣貴成雅俗；

translations.literal: At court many gentlemen have already honored and perfected custom;
translations.idiomatic: At court many gentlemen have already honored and perfected custom;

sentences.zh: 野有外臣，宜弘此難進。

translations.literal: in the wild there are outer ministers—this hard-to-advance should be enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: in the wild there are outer ministers—this hard-to-advance path should be enlarged.

sentences.zh: 方賴清徽，式隆大業。

translations.literal: I was about to rely on your pure emblem to loft the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I was about to rely on your pure emblem to loft the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 昔在布衣，情期早著，資以仲虞之秩，待以子陵之禮，聽覽暇日，角巾引見，窅然汾射，茲焉有託。

translations.literal: Long ago in plain cloth our feeling was pledged early; I endowed you with Zhongyu's rank and treated you with Ziling's rites; on days of leisure for reading I received you in kerchief—remote as Fen and She, here was my trust.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago in plain cloth our bond was early; I gave you Zhongyu's rank and Ziling's rites; on days of leisure I received you in kerchief—remote as Fen and She, here was my trust.

sentences.zh: 一旦萬古，良懷震悼。

translations.literal: In one morning ten thousand years—my good heart is shaken with mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In one morning ten thousand years—my heart is shaken with mourning.

sentences.zh: 卿友於純至，親從凋亡；

translations.literal: You were friendly in pure utmost; kin and followers have withered;
translations.idiomatic: You were friendly in pure utmost; kin and followers have withered;

sentences.zh: 偕老之願，致使反奪；

translations.literal: the wish to grow old together makes the reversal all the harder;
translations.idiomatic: the wish to grow old together makes the reversal all the harder;

sentences.zh: 纏綿永恨，伊何可任。

translations.literal: enduring regret wound tight—how can it be borne?
translations.idiomatic: enduring regret wound tight—how can it be borne?

sentences.zh: 永矣柰何！

translations.literal: Gone forever—what can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Gone forever—what can be done!"

sentences.zh: 」點無子，宗人以其從弟耿子遲任爲嗣。

translations.literal: Dian had no son; the clan made his younger cousin Geng's son Chi heir.
translations.idiomatic: Dian had no son; the clan made his younger cousin Geng's son Chi heir.

sentences.zh: 胤字子季，點之弟也。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Ziji, was Dian's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Ziji, was Dian's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，居憂哀毀若成人。

translations.literal: At eight sui in mourning he grieved and wasted himself like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he mourned with grief and waste like an adult.

sentences.zh: 旣長好學。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning.

sentences.zh: 師事沛國劉瓛，受《易》及《禮記》、《毛詩》，又入鐘山定林寺聽內典，其業皆通。

translations.literal: He took Liu Huan of Pei as teacher, receiving the Changes, the Record of Rites, and the Mao Odes, and also entered Dinglin Temple on Bell Mountain to hear the inner canon—all his studies he mastered.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Huan of Pei, taking the Changes, the Record of Rites, and the Mao Odes, and entered Dinglin Temple on Bell Mountain for the inner canon—mastering all.

sentences.zh: 而縱情誕節，時人未之知也，唯瓛與汝南周顒深器異之。

translations.literal: Yet he gave free rein to wild conduct; men of the time did not yet know him—only Huan and Zhou Yong of Runan deeply prized and marked him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gave free rein to wild conduct; his age did not yet know him—only Huan and Zhou Yong of Runan deeply prized him.

sentences.zh: 起家齊秘書郎，遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: He first left home as Qi Secretary in the Palace, moved to Crown Prince's Household Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He first left home as Qi secretary in the palace and became crown prince's household attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲建安太守，爲政有恩信，民不忍欺。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Jian'an; his rule had grace and trust, and the people could not bear to deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as Jian'an administrator, he ruled with grace and trust, and the people would not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 每伏臘放囚還家，依期而返。

translations.literal: At every Fu and La festival he released prisoners to go home, and they returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Each Fu and La he sent prisoners home, and they came back on time.

sentences.zh: 入爲尚書三公郎，不拜，遷司徒主簿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Secretariat aide to the Three Excellencies but did not accept; he was transferred to Registrar of the Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Secretariat aide to the Three Excellencies, declined, and became registrar of the Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 注《易》，又解《禮記》，於卷背書之，謂爲《隱義》。

translations.literal: He annotated the *Changes* and also explicated the *Record of Rites*, writing on the back of the scrolls—calling it *Hidden Meanings*.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the *Changes* and explicated the *Record of Rites* on scroll backs, titling the work *Hidden Meanings*.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書郎、員外散騎常侍、太尉從事中郎、司徒右長史、給事黃門侍郎、太子中庶子、領國子博士、丹陽邑中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted through Central Secretariat Gentleman, Supernumerary Regular Attendant, Secretariat aide to the Grand Marshal, Right Chief Clerk to the Minister of Rites, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent, concurrent Erudite of the National University, and Rectifier of Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through secretariat gentleman, supernumerary attendant, grand marshal aide, right chief clerk, yellow-gates gentleman, heir-apparent aide, national university erudite, and Danyang rectifier.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉受詔撰新禮，未就而卒。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian received the decree to compile the new rites but died before finishing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, director of the Masters of Writing, was ordered to draft the new rites but died unfinished.

sentences.zh: 又使特進張緒續成之，緒又卒；

translations.literal: They then had Specially Promoted Zhang Xu continue it, and Xu also died;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu, specially promoted, was set to finish it, and he too died;

sentences.zh: 屬在司徒竟陵王子良，子良以讓胤，乃置學士二十人，佐胤撰錄。

translations.literal: The task fell to Minister of Rites Prince Ziliang of Jingling; Ziliang yielded it to Yin, set up twenty academic officers, and had them assist Yin in compiling and editing.
translations.idiomatic: It fell to Minister of Rites Prince Ziliang of Jingling; Ziliang gave it to Yin, appointed twenty scholars, and had them help Yin compile.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，遷侍中，領步兵校尉，轉爲國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In Yongming year ten he was promoted to Palace Attendant, concurrent Colonel of Footsoldiers, and then became Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming year ten he became palace attendant and colonel of footsoldiers, then chancellor of the national university.

sentences.zh: 鬱林嗣位，胤爲后族，甚見親待。

translations.literal: When Yulin succeeded to the throne, Yin was kin to the empress and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin succeeded, Yin was the empress's kin and was treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷左民尚書、領驍騎、中書令、領臨海、巴陵王師。

translations.literal: He was promoted through Minister of the People for the Left, concurrent Commander of Agile Cavalry, Director of the Secretariat, and concurrent Tutor to the Princes of Linhai and Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through left minister of the people, agile-cavalry commander, director of the secretariat, and tutor to the princes of Linhai and Baling.

sentences.zh: 胤雖貴顯，常懷止足。

translations.literal: Though Yin was noble and prominent, he always cherished knowing when to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Though noble and prominent, Yin always knew when enough was enough.

sentences.zh: 建武初，已築室郊外，號曰小山，恒與學徒游處其內。

translations.literal: Early in Jianwu he had already built a house in the suburbs called Little Hill, and constantly wandered and lived within it with his students.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jianwu he had built a suburban house called Little Hill and constantly lived there with his students.

sentences.zh: 至是，遂賣園宅，欲入東山，未及發，聞謝朏罷吳興郡不還，胤恐後之，乃拜表辭職，不待報輒去。

translations.literal: At this point he sold his garden and house, intending to enter Eastern Hills; before he could set out, he heard Xie Tiao had left the grand administration of Wuxing and would not return—Yin feared being too late, submitted a memorial resigning office, and left without waiting for a reply.
translations.idiomatic: He sold his estate to enter Eastern Hills; before leaving he heard Xie Tiao had quit Wuxing and would not return—fearing to be second, Yin resigned and left without waiting for approval.

sentences.zh: 明帝大怒，使御史中丞袁昂奏收胤，尋有詔許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was greatly angry and had Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yuan Ang memorialize to seize Yin; soon an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming raged and had vice director Yuan Ang move to arrest Yin; soon an edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 胤以會稽山多靈異，往游焉，居若邪山雲門寺。

translations.literal: Yin found Kuaiji's mountains rich in spiritual marvels, traveled there, and dwelt at Cloud Gate Monastery on Mt Ruoye.
translations.idiomatic: Yin found Kuaiji's mountains full of wonders, traveled there, and lived at Cloud Gate Monastery on Mt Ruoye.

sentences.zh: 初，胤二兄求、點並棲遁，求先卒，至是胤又隱，世號點爲大山；

translations.literal: Earlier Yin's two elder brothers Qiu and Dian had both lived in reclusion; Qiu died first, and now Yin too withdrew—the age called Dian Great Hill;
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Qiu and Dian had both recluded; Qiu died first, and now Yin withdrew too—the age called Dian Great Hill;

sentences.zh: 胤爲小山，亦曰東山。

translations.literal: Yin Little Hill, also called Eastern Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was Little Hill, also called Eastern Hills.

sentences.zh: 永元中，徵太常、太子詹事，並不就。

translations.literal: In the Yongyuan era he was summoned as Grand Commandant and Steward to the Heir Apparent—he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan he was summoned as grand commandant and heir-apparent steward and accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 高祖霸府建，引胤爲軍謀祭酒，與書曰：「想恒清豫，縱情林壑，致足歡也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu established the Hegemon's Office he invited Yin as Libationer for Army Planning and wrote to him: "I imagine you are ever serene and at ease, giving free rein to feeling amid forests and ravines—altogether enough for joy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu set up the hegemon's office he made Yin army-planning libationer and wrote: "I imagine you are always serene, roaming forests and ravines—joy enough.

sentences.zh: 旣內絕心戰，外勞物役，以道養和，履候無爽。

translations.literal: Having inwardly renounced the heart of strife and outwardly spared yourself the toil of things, you nurture harmony by the Way; your tread in season is never amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly you have dropped strife, outwardly you spare toil; you nourish harmony by the Way and keep every season without fault.

sentences.zh: 若邪擅美東區，山川相屬，前世嘉賞，是爲樂土。

translations.literal: Ruoye monopolizes the beauty of the eastern region, mountains and streams linked in succession—a land praised by former ages, truly a happy soil.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoye holds the east's beauty, mountains and streams unbroken, praised by former ages—a happy land.

sentences.zh: 僕推遷簿官，自東徂西，悟言素對，用成睽闋，傾首東顧，曷日無懷。

translations.literal: I have been pushed through petty official posts from east to west; our plain-spoken meetings became estrangement; I crane my neck looking east—what day is without longing?
translations.idiomatic: I have been shuffled through petty posts east to west; our talks became estrangement; I look east every day without end of longing.

sentences.zh: 疇昔歡遇，曳裾儒肆，實欲臥遊千載，畋漁百氏，一行爲吏，此事遂乖。

translations.literal: In former happy meetings we trailed robes in the halls of scholars, truly wishing to travel a thousand years in repose and hunt and fish among the hundred schools—but one turn into office, and this was betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: Once we trailed robes in the halls of learning, wishing to roam a thousand years in books and hunt the hundred schools—but one turn to office ended it.

sentences.zh: 屬以世道威夷，仍離屯故，投袂數千，剋黜釁禍。

translations.literal: Just then the age's might was crushed, we again left our base of fortune; I shook my sleeves with thousands and overcame the bale of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Then the age's might was broken and we left our base; I rallied thousands and put down disaster.

sentences.zh: 思得矚卷諮款，寓情古昔，夫豈不懷，事與願謝。

translations.literal: I thought to gain your glance upon my scrolls and intimate counsel, to lodge feeling in the past—how could I not long for it? Yet affairs and wishes parted.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to read your scrolls and speak heart to heart of the past—how could I not long for it? Yet affairs and wishes parted.

sentences.zh: 君清襟素托，棲寄不近，中居人世，殆同隱淪。

translations.literal: Your pure breast and simple trust, dwelling-place not near—the midst of the human world, nearly the same as hidden withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Your pure heart and simple trust, dwelling not near the court—in the human world you are nearly a recluse.

sentences.zh: 旣俯拾青組，又脫屣硃黻。

translations.literal: You have both stooped to pick up green ribbons and cast off vermilion robes like shoes.
translations.idiomatic: You have both taken up green ribbons and cast off vermilion rank like shoes.

sentences.zh: 但理存用捨，義貴隨時，往識禍萌，實爲先覺，超然獨善，有識欽嗟。

translations.literal: Yet principle lies in use and rejection, righteousness honors timeliness; recognizing calamity's sprout before, you were truly foreknowing—transcendent in solitary goodness, the knowing admire and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Yet principle is use and rejection, righteousness is timeliness; you saw calamity coming and stood apart in goodness—the knowing admire you.

sentences.zh: 今者爲邦，貧賤咸恥，好仁由己，幸無凝滯。

translations.literal: Today in governing the state, poor and lowly alike feel shame; loving benevolence is up to oneself—by fortune do not hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: Today to serve the state, even the poor feel shame if they do not love benevolence—do not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 比別具白，此未盡言。

translations.literal: On another occasion I shall set this forth in detail; this does not exhaust the words.
translations.idiomatic: I will explain more elsewhere; this letter does not say all.

sentences.zh: 今遣候承音息，矯首還翰，慰其引領。

translations.literal: Now I send an envoy to receive your news; crane your neck and return a letter, to comfort this craning forward.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send a messenger for your word; look up and write back to ease my waiting.

sentences.zh: 」胤不至。

translations.literal: Yin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not come.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，詔爲特進、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he decreed Yin Specially Promoted and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he made Yin specially promoted and right grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 手敕曰：「吾猥當期運，膺此樂推，而顧己蒙蔽，昧於治道。

translations.literal: A handwritten edict said: "I unworthily met the destined era and received this joyous elevation, yet looking at myself I am benighted and obscure in the way of rule.
translations.idiomatic: A handwritten edict said: "I unworthily met the age and received elevation, yet I am benighted in the way of rule.

sentences.zh: 雖復劬勞日昃，思致隆平，而先王遺范，尚蘊方策，自舉之用，存乎其人。

translations.literal: Though I toil from sun to sun and think to bring abundant peace, the former kings' bequeathed models still lie hidden in the policy scrolls—the use of self-recommendation rests in the man.
translations.idiomatic: Though I toil from sun to sun seeking peace, the former kings' models lie in the scrolls—who is raised depends on the man.

sentences.zh: 兼以世道澆暮，爭詐繁起，改俗遷風，良有未易。

translations.literal: Moreover the age's ways are thin and twilight; contention and fraud flourish—changing custom and shifting wind is truly not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the age is thin and deceit flourishes—changing custom is not easy.

sentences.zh: 自非以儒雅弘朝，高尚軌物，則汩流所至，莫知其限。

translations.literal: Unless by Confucian elegance to magnify the court and lofty standards to guide things, then wherever the muddy current runs none knows its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Confucian elegance exalts the court and lofty standards guide things, the muddy current has no limit.

sentences.zh: 治人之與治身，獨善之與兼濟，得失去取，爲用孰多。

translations.literal: Governing others versus governing the self, solitary goodness versus aiding all—gain, loss, taking, leaving—which use is greater?
translations.idiomatic: Governing others or the self, solitary good or aiding all—which matters more?

sentences.zh: 吾雖不學，頗好博古，尚想高塵，每懷擊節。

translations.literal: Though I do not study, I rather love probing antiquity, still think on lofty dust, and ever cherish beating the measure.
translations.idiomatic: Though I do not study, I love antiquity, still think on lofty men, and beat the measure in admiration.

sentences.zh: 今世務紛亂，憂責是當，不得不屈道岩阿，共成世美。

translations.literal: Today's affairs are tangled and confused; anxiety and duty are fitting—you cannot but bend the Way to cliff and dell and together complete the age's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Today affairs are tangled; duty calls—you must bend the Way to the cliffs and help complete the age's beauty.

sentences.zh: 必望深達往懷，不吝濡足。

translations.literal: I surely hope you deeply reach my former feeling and do not stint wetting your feet.
translations.idiomatic: I hope you understand my old wish and do not refuse to wet your feet.

sentences.zh: 今遣領軍司馬王果宣旨諭意，遲面在近。

translations.literal: Now I send Army-inspecting Chief-of-Staff Wang Guo to announce the intent and explain my meaning—meeting face to face is near.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send army-inspecting chief Wang Guo to announce my meaning—we shall meet soon.

sentences.zh: 」果至，胤單衣鹿巾，執經卷，下床跪受詔書，就席伏讀。

translations.literal: " When Guo arrived, Yin wore a single robe and deer-cloth cap, held a classic scroll, came down from his couch to kneel and receive the edict, then returned to his seat and read prone.
translations.idiomatic: Guo arrived; Yin wore a single robe and deer cap, held a classic scroll, knelt to receive the edict, then read it prone at his seat.

sentences.zh: 胤因謂果曰：「吾昔於齊朝欲陳兩三條事，一者欲正郊丘，二者欲更鑄九鼎，三者欲樹雙闕。

translations.literal: Yin then said to Guo: "In the Qi court I once wished to present two or three points: first to correct the suburban altar and mound; second to recast the Nine Tripods; third to raise twin gate-towers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin told Guo: "In Qi I wished to present three things: correct the suburban altar and mound, recast the nine tripods, and raise twin gate-towers.

sentences.zh: 世傳晉室欲立闕，王丞相指牛頭山云：『此天闕也』，是則未明立闕之意。

translations.literal: Tradition says the Jin house wished to raise gate-towers; Chief Minister Wang pointed at Ox Head Mountain and said, "This is Heaven's tower"—thus they did not clarify the meaning of raising towers.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition says Jin wished to raise towers; Chief Minister Wang pointed at Ox Head Mountain and said "This is Heaven's tower"—they never understood what a tower was for.

sentences.zh: 闕者，謂之象魏。

translations.literal: A gate-tower is what is called the Elephant-Dawning.
translations.idiomatic: A tower is called the Elephant-Dawning.

sentences.zh: 縣象法於其上，浹日而收之。

translations.literal: Laws and standards are hung upon it; at the sun's fullness they are gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: Laws are displayed on it and gathered in at the full of day.

sentences.zh: 象者，法也；

translations.literal: "Elephant" means law;
translations.idiomatic: "Elephant" means law;

sentences.zh: 魏者，當塗而高大貌也。

translations.literal: "Dawning" means the appearance of towering height on the road of rule.
translations.idiomatic: "Dawning" means towering height on the road of rule.

sentences.zh: 鼎者神器，有國所先，故王孫滿斥言，楚子頓盡。

translations.literal: The tripod is the sacred vessel, what those with a state put first—hence Wangsun Man's stern words and the Chu lord's meal brought to a halt.
translations.idiomatic: The tripod is the sacred vessel states put first—hence Wangsun Man's rebuke and the Chu lord's feast cut short.

sentences.zh: 圓丘國郊，舊典不同。

translations.literal: Round Mound and state suburban sacrifice—in the old canons they differed.
translations.idiomatic: Round Mound and state suburban rites differed in the old canons.

sentences.zh: 南郊祠五帝靈威仰之類，圓丘祠天皇大帝、北極大星是也。

translations.literal: The southern suburban sacrifices to the Five Thearchs, Spiritual Majesty Yang, and the like; the Round Mound sacrifices to the Celestial Sovereign Great Thearch and the Pole Star—that is the distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The southern suburb sacrifices to the Five Thearchs and Spiritual Majesty Yang; the Round Mound to the Celestial Sovereign and Pole Star—that is the distinction.

sentences.zh: 往代合之郊丘，先儒之巨失。

translations.literal: Former ages merged suburban and mound sacrifices—a great error of the early Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Merging suburb and mound was a great error of the early Confucians.

sentences.zh: 今梁德告始，不宜遂因前謬。

translations.literal: Now Liang's virtue is newly proclaimed; one should not straightway follow the former error.
translations.idiomatic: Now Liang's virtue begins; we should not follow the old error.

sentences.zh: 卿宜詣闕陳之。

translations.literal: You should go to the palace and present this.
translations.idiomatic: You should go to court and present this.

sentences.zh: 」果曰：「僕之鄙劣，豈敢輕議國典？

translations.literal: " Guo said: "This servant is crude and inferior—how dare I lightly discuss state canons?
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "I am crude and low—how dare I discuss state canons?

sentences.zh: 此當敬俟叔孫生耳。

translations.literal: This should respectfully await a Master Shu Sun."
translations.idiomatic: That should await a Master Shu Sun."

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「卿詎不遣傳詔還朝拜表，留與我同遊邪？

translations.literal: " Yin said: "Will you not send the edict-bearer back to court with a memorial and stay to wander with me?
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "Will you not send the messenger back with a memorial and stay to roam with me?

sentences.zh: 」果愕然曰：「古今不聞此例。

translations.literal: " Guo said in astonishment: "Past and present have not heard this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Guo said in astonishment: "Past and present have no such precedent.

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「《檀弓》兩卷，皆言物始。

translations.literal: " Yin said: "The two scrolls of *Tann Gong* all speak of things' beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "The two scrolls of *Tann Gong* all speak of beginnings.

sentences.zh: 自卿而始，何必有例。

translations.literal: Beginning from you—why must there be a precedent?
translations.idiomatic: Begin with you—why need a precedent?

sentences.zh: 」果曰：「今君遂當邈然絕世，猶有致身理不？

translations.literal: " Guo said: "Now you are to withdraw utterly from the world—is there still any principle of taking office?
translations.idiomatic: Guo said: "Now you withdraw from the world—is there still any reason to take office?

sentences.zh: 」胤曰：「卿但以事見推，吾年已五十七，月食四斗米不盡，何容得有宦情？

translations.literal: " Yin said: "You only push me with affairs; I am already fifty-seven, and four pecks of rice a month do not finish—how could I harbor desire for office?
translations.idiomatic: Yin said: "You only push me with business; I am fifty-seven, and four pecks of rice a month do not finish me—how could I want office?

sentences.zh: 昔荷聖王跂識，今又蒙旌賁，甚願詣闕謝恩，但比腰腳大惡，此心不遂耳。」

translations.literal: Formerly I bore the sage king's eager recognition; now again I receive honoring reward—I very much wish to go to court and thank grace, but lately my waist and legs are greatly afflicted, and this heart cannot be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Once the sage king favored me; now I am honored again—I wish to thank at court, but my waist and legs are too bad, and this heart cannot be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 果還，以胤意奏聞，有敕給白衣尚書祿，胤固辭。

translations.literal: Guo returned and reported Yin's meaning; an edict granted the salary of a Masters of Writing in plain robes—Yin firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Guo returned and reported; an edict granted plain-robes masters-of-writing salary—Yin firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又敕山陰庫錢月給五萬，胤又不受。

translations.literal: Again an edict gave fifty thousand from the Shanyin treasury each month—Yin again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Again fifty thousand from the Shanyin treasury each month—Yin again refused.

sentences.zh: 乃敕胤曰：「頃者學業淪廢，儒術將盡，閭閻搢紳，鮮聞好事。

translations.literal: Then an edict to Yin said: "Recently learning has sunk and been abandoned, Confucian arts are nearly exhausted; in lanes and wards among gentry and officials, few are heard doing good.
translations.idiomatic: Then an edict to Yin said: "Learning has lately sunk and Confucian arts nearly end; in lanes and wards few gentry are heard doing good.

sentences.zh: 吾每思弘獎，其風未移，當扆興言爲歎。

translations.literal: I ever think to expand and encourage, yet the wind does not shift—I sigh when I rise to speak at the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I ever wish to encourage it, yet the wind does not change—I sigh at the throne.

sentences.zh: 本欲屈卿暫出，開導後生，旣屬廢業，此懷未遂，延佇之勞，載盈夢想。

translations.literal: I originally wished to bend you to come out briefly and open and guide the younger generation; since learning has been abandoned, this wish is unfulfilled—the labor of waiting fills my dreams.
translations.idiomatic: I wished you would come out briefly and guide the young; since learning is abandoned, this wish fails—the wait fills my dreams.

sentences.zh: 理舟虛席，須俟來秋，所望惠然，申其宿抱耳。

translations.literal: I ready the boat and empty the seat, waiting till next autumn; what I hope is your gracious coming to voice the long-held embrace.
translations.idiomatic: I ready the boat and empty the seat for next autumn; I hope you will come and speak the wish long held.

sentences.zh: 卿門徒中經明行脩，厥數有幾？

translations.literal: Among your disciples, how many are clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct?
translations.idiomatic: Among your disciples, how many are clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct?

sentences.zh: 且欲瞻彼堂堂，置此周行。

translations.literal: I also wish to behold those stately ones and set them in this grand procession.
translations.idiomatic: I also wish to see the stately ones and set them in the grand procession.

sentences.zh: 便可具以名聞，副其勞望。

translations.literal: You may at once submit their names in full, matching their labor and hope.
translations.idiomatic: Submit their names at once to match their labor and hope.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「比歲學者殊爲寡少，良由無復聚徒，故明經斯廢。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In recent years scholars are especially few—truly because there is no longer gathering of disciples, thus mastery of the classics is abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Scholars are especially few lately—because there are no more gathered disciples, mastery of the classics is abandoned.

sentences.zh: 每一念此，爲之慨然。

translations.literal: Each time I think of this I sigh for it.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I think of this I sigh.

sentences.zh: 卿居儒宗，加以德素，當敕後進有意向者，就卿受業。

translations.literal: You stand at the head of Confucian teaching, moreover with plain virtue—you should order those among the later ranks who have intent to come study under you.
translations.idiomatic: You are head of Confucian teaching and plain in virtue—order those among the young who wish it to study under you.

sentences.zh: 想深思誨誘，使斯文載興。

translations.literal: I trust you will deeply ponder, teach, and entice, and make this civilization rise again.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you will teach and entice deeply and make this civilization rise again.

sentences.zh: 」於是遣何子朗、孔壽等六人於東山受學。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sent He Zilang, Kong Shou, and six others to study on Eastern Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sent He Zilang, Kong Shou, and six others to study on Eastern Hills.

sentences.zh: 太守衡陽王元簡深加禮敬，月中常命駕式閭，談論終日。

translations.literal: The grand administrator, Prince Yuan Jian of Hengyang, deeply honored him; each month he often ordered his carriage to call at his lane and discussed all day.
translations.idiomatic: Grand administrator Prince Yuan Jian of Hengyang deeply honored him; each month he often drove to his lane and talked all day.

sentences.zh: 胤以若邪處勢迫隘，不容生徒，乃遷秦望山。

translations.literal: Yin found Ruoye's site cramped by terrain and unable to hold students, so he moved to Mt Qinwang.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoye was cramped and could not hold students, so Yin moved to Mt Qinwang.

sentences.zh: 山有飛泉，西起學舍，卽林成援，因岩爲堵。

translations.literal: The mountain had a flying spring; westward he raised a study hall, taking the forest as post and the cliff as wall.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain had a flying spring; westward he built a study hall, the forest as posts and the cliff as wall.

sentences.zh: 別爲小閤室，寢處其中，躬自啓閉，僮僕無得至者。

translations.literal: He made a separate small chamber for sleeping, opened and closed it himself—servants could not reach it.
translations.idiomatic: He made a small sleeping chamber, opened and closed it himself—servants could not enter.

sentences.zh: 山側營田二頃，講隙從生徒遊之。

translations.literal: On the mountainside he farmed two qing; between lectures he strolled there with his students.
translations.idiomatic: On the mountainside he farmed two qing; between lectures he walked there with students.

sentences.zh: 胤初遷，將築室，忽見二人著玄冠，容貌甚偉，問胤曰：「君欲居此邪？

translations.literal: When Yin first moved and was about to build a house, he suddenly saw two men in black caps, countenances very imposing, who asked Yin: "Do you wish to dwell here?
translations.idiomatic: When Yin first moved to build, he suddenly saw two men in black caps, very imposing, who asked: "Do you wish to live here?

sentences.zh: 」乃指一處云：「此中殊吉。

translations.literal: " Then pointing to a place they said: "This spot is especially auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to a place they said: "This spot is especially auspicious.

sentences.zh: 」忽不復見，胤依其言而止焉。

translations.literal: " Suddenly they were gone; Yin followed their words and stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly they vanished; Yin followed their words and stopped there.

sentences.zh: 尋而山發洪水，樹石皆倒拔，唯胤所居室巋然獨存。

translations.literal: Soon the mountain sent forth flood-waters; trees and stones were all uprooted—only Yin's dwelling stood massive and alone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the mountain flooded; trees and stones were uprooted—only Yin's house stood intact.

sentences.zh: 元簡乃命記室參軍鐘嶸作《瑞室頌》，刻石以旌之。

translations.literal: Yuan Jian then had his Recorder-of-the-Army Attendant Zhong Rong compose "Ode on the Auspicious Chamber" and carved stone to honor it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jian had recorder Zhong Rong compose "Ode on the Auspicious Chamber" and carved stone to honor it.

sentences.zh: 及元簡去郡，入山與胤別，送至都賜埭，去郡三里，因曰：「僕自棄人事，交遊路斷，自非降貴山藪，豈容復望城邑？

translations.literal: When Yuan Jian left the commandery he entered the mountains to bid Yin farewell, escorting him to Capital Gift Dam three li from the commandery, and said: "I myself have cast off human affairs and cut off the road of friendship—unless nobles descend to mountain and marsh, how could I again look on cities and towns?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Jian left the commandery he entered the hills to bid Yin farewell, escorting him to Capital Gift Dam three li out, and said: "I have cast off human affairs and cut off friendship—unless nobles descend to the hills, how could I look on cities again?

sentences.zh: 此埭之游，於今絕矣。

translations.literal: This dam outing ends today.
translations.idiomatic: This dam outing ends today.

sentences.zh: 」執手涕零。

translations.literal: " They clasped hands with tears streaming.
translations.idiomatic: They clasped hands in tears.

sentences.zh: 何氏過江，自晉司空充並葬吳西山。

translations.literal: The He clan crossed the river; from Jin's Minister of Works Chong onward all were buried on Western Hill of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The He clan crossed the river; from Jin minister of works Chong onward all were buried on Wu's Western Hill.

sentences.zh: 胤家世年皆不永，唯祖尚之至七十二。

translations.literal: In Yin's family each generation's years were not long—only grandfather Shangzhi reached seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's family never lived long—only grandfather Shangzhi reached seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 胤年登祖壽，乃移還吳，作《別山詩》一首，言甚悽愴。

translations.literal: When Yin's years reached his grandfather's span he moved back to Wu, composed one poem "Farewell to the Mountains," the words very mournful.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin reached his grandfather's span he moved back to Wu and wrote "Farewell to the Mountains," very mournful.

sentences.zh: 至吳，居虎丘西寺講經論，學徒復隨之，東境守宰經途者，莫不畢至。

translations.literal: Reaching Wu he dwelt at Tiger Hill West Monastery lecturing on classics and treatises; students again followed him, and magistrates along the eastern circuit's routes all came without exception.
translations.idiomatic: At Wu he lived at Tiger Hill West Monastery lecturing on classics; students followed, and eastern magistrates on the road all came.

sentences.zh: 胤常禁殺，有虞人逐鹿，鹿徑來趨胤，伏而不動。

translations.literal: Yin always forbade killing; a gamekeeper chased a deer that came straight to Yin, crouched, and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Yin always forbade killing; a gamekeeper chased a deer that ran straight to Yin, crouched, and did not move.

sentences.zh: 又有異鳥如鶴，紅色，集講堂，馴狎如家禽焉。

translations.literal: There was also a strange bird like a crane, red in color, that settled in the lecture hall and was tame as domestic fowl.
translations.idiomatic: A strange red crane-like bird settled in the lecture hall, tame as poultry.

sentences.zh: 初，開善寺藏法師與胤遇於秦望，後還都，卒於鐘山。

translations.literal: Earlier the monk Zang of Kaishan Monastery had met Yin on Mt Qinwang; later he returned to the capital and died on Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier monk Zang of Kaishan Monastery met Yin on Mt Qinwang; later he returned to the capital and died on Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 其死日，胤在般若寺，見一僧授胤香奩並函書，云「呈何居士」，言訖失所在。

translations.literal: On the day of his death Yin was at Prajna Monastery, saw a monk hand Yin an incense casket and boxed letter saying "Presented to Layman He," and when the words ended he vanished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died Yin was at Prajna Monastery; a monk gave Yin an incense casket and boxed letter saying "For Layman He," then vanished.

sentences.zh: 胤開函，乃是《大莊嚴論》，世中未有。

translations.literal: Yin opened the case: inside was the *Treatise on the Great Majestic*, not yet known in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yin opened the box and found the *Treatise on the Great Majestic*—unknown anywhere in the world.

sentences.zh: 又於寺內立明珠柱，乃七日七夜放光，太守何遠以狀啓。

translations.literal: They also set up a pearl pillar in the temple; for seven days and nights it shone, and Governor He Yuan reported the matter in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: A pearl pillar was raised in the temple and glowed seven days and nights; Governor He Yuan memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子欽其德，遣舍人何思澄致手令以褒美之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming admired his virtue and sent Gentleman of the Household He Sicheng with a personal letter of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming, honoring his virtue, sent He Sicheng with a handwritten commendation.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，卒，年八十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong he died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Zhongdatong, at eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 先是胤疾，妻江氏夢神人告之曰：「汝夫壽盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yin fell ill, his wife Lady Jiang dreamed that a spirit told her: "Your husband's allotted span is finished.
translations.idiomatic: Before his death, while Yin was ill, Lady Jiang dreamed a spirit say, "Your husband's life is spent.

sentences.zh: 旣有至德，應獲延期，爾當代之。

translations.literal: Because he has reached virtue, he should receive an extension; you must take his place."
translations.idiomatic: His virtue merits a reprieve—you must die in his stead."

sentences.zh: 」妻覺說焉，俄得患而卒，胤疾乃瘳。

translations.literal: The wife woke and told him; soon she fell ill and died, and Yin's sickness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: She told him on waking; soon she sickened and died, and Yin recovered.

sentences.zh: 至是胤夢一神女，幷八十許人，並衣帢，行列至前，俱拜床下，覺又見之，便命營凶具。

translations.literal: By then Yin dreamed a goddess with some eighty attendants, all in headcloths, marching in ranks to his bed and bowing together; waking, he saw them again and ordered funeral goods prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Then he dreamed a goddess and eighty attendants in headcloths, ranked before his bed and bowing; waking he saw them again and ordered his coffin made.

sentences.zh: 旣而疾動，因不自治。

translations.literal: Soon his illness worsened and he could no longer care for himself.
translations.idiomatic: His illness soon worsened beyond his power to tend it.

sentences.zh: 胤注《百法論》、《十二門論》各一卷，注《周易》十卷、《毛詩總集》六卷、《毛詩隱義》十卷、《禮記隱義》二十卷、《禮答問》五十五卷。

translations.literal: Yin annotated the *Hundred Dharmas Treatise* and the *Twelve Gates Treatise*, one scroll each; annotated the *Book of Changes* in ten scrolls, the *General Collection of the Mao Odes* in six, the *Hidden Meanings of the Mao Odes* in ten, the *Hidden Meanings of the Book of Rites* in twenty, and *Ritual Questions Answered* in fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote commentaries: one scroll each on the *Hundred Dharmas* and *Twelve Gates*; ten on the *Changes*; six on the Mao odes; ten on their hidden meanings; twenty on ritual hidden meanings; fifty-five of ritual Q and A.

sentences.zh: 子撰，亦不仕，廬陵王辟爲主簿，不就。

translations.literal: His son Zhuan also refused office; Prince of Luling summoned him as chief clerk, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhuan would not serve either; the Prince of Luling made him chief clerk, and he declined.

sentences.zh: 阮孝緒

translations.literal: Ruan Xiaoxu
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiaoxu

sentences.zh: 阮孝緒字士宗，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Xiaoxu, styled Shizong, was a man of Wei county in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiaoxu, styled Shizong, came from Wei in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 父彥之，宋太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi was attendant gentleman in the Song Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi served as attendant gentleman to the Song Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 孝緒七歲，出後從伯胤之。

translations.literal: At seven, Xiaoxu was given in adoption to his father's cousin Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was adopted by his father's cousin Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 胤之母周氏卒，有遺財百餘萬，應歸孝緒，孝緒一無所納，盡以歸胤之姊琅邪王晏之母，聞者咸歎異之。

translations.literal: When Yinzhi's mother Lady Zhou died, more than a million in legacy property should have gone to Xiaoxu; he accepted none of it and gave all to Yinzhi's sister, mother of Wang Yan of Langya—all who heard it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinzhi's mother died, a million-plus legacy was Xiaoxu's by right; he took nothing and gave all to Yinzhi's sister, Wang Yan's mother—hearers marveled.

sentences.zh: 幼至孝，性沉靜，雖與兒童遊戲，恒以穿池築山爲樂。

translations.literal: From childhood he was utmost in filial piety and quiet by nature; even playing with other children, he always took delight in digging ponds and piling hills.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and withdrawn from childhood, he played only at digging ponds and building miniature mountains.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遍通《五經》。

translations.literal: At thirteen he had mastered the Five Classics throughout.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he had read through the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 十五，冠而見其父，彥之誡曰：「三加彌尊，人倫之始。

translations.literal: At fifteen, capped, he was presented to his father; Yanzhi admonished him: "Three times capped, ever more honored—this is the beginning of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Capped at fifteen and presented to his father, Yanzhi warned him: "Three investitures, growing honor—that is where human duty begins.

sentences.zh: 宜思自勖，以庇爾躬。

translations.literal: You should strive to strengthen yourself to shelter your own person."
translations.idiomatic: Strive to brace yourself and shelter your own life."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「願迹松子於瀛海，追許由於穹谷，庶保促生，以免塵累。

translations.literal: He answered: "I wish to follow Master Zi on the eastern sea and Xu You in the deep valley, hoping to keep my life short and escape the dust of the world."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I would trace Master Zi on the eastern sea and Xu You in the deep valley, keep my life brief, and slip the world's dust."

sentences.zh: 」自是屏居一室，非定省未嘗出戶，家人莫見其面，親友因呼爲「居士」。

translations.literal: From then on he shut himself in one room and would not step outside except for the fixed visits to his parents; the household scarcely saw his face, and kin and friends therefore called him "the Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself in one room, leaving only for obligatory visits to his parents; kin called him "the Recluse," for none saw his face.

sentences.zh: 外兄王晏貴顯，屢至其門，孝緒度之必至顛覆，常逃匿不與相見。

translations.literal: His cousin by marriage Wang Yan was powerful and visited his gate again and again; Xiaoxu gauged that Yan would surely fall and constantly hid himself, refusing to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Wang Yan, risen high, came often; Xiaoxu foresaw his ruin and hid, refusing every meeting.

sentences.zh: 曾食醬美，問之，云是王家所得，便吐飧覆醢。

translations.literal: Once he ate a tasty sauce; asked where it came from, he was told the Wang household had sent it, and he vomited the meal and overturned the relish.
translations.idiomatic: He once ate a fine sauce; learning it came from the Wangs, he vomited his meal and dashed the dish aside.

sentences.zh: 及晏誅，其親戚咸爲之懼，孝緒曰：「親而不黨，何坐之及？

translations.literal: When Yan was executed, his kinsmen were all afraid for themselves; Xiaoxu said, "Love kin but do not take their party—why should guilt reach me?"
translations.idiomatic: At Yan's execution his kin trembled; Xiaoxu said, "One may love kin without siding with them—why would I be punished?"

sentences.zh: 」竟獲免。

translations.literal: In the end he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He was spared after all.

sentences.zh: 義師圍京城，家貧無以爨，僮妾竊鄰人樵以繼火。

translations.literal: When the righteous army besieged the capital, the household was too poor to cook; a servant secretly took a neighbor's firewood to keep the fire going.
translations.idiomatic: As the righteous army besieged the capital, they were too poor to cook; a servant stole a neighbor's firewood to feed the hearth.

sentences.zh: 孝緒知之，乃不食，更令撤屋而炊。

translations.literal: When Xiaoxu learned of it, he would not eat and had them pull down the house to burn for fuel.
translations.idiomatic: Learning this, he refused food and had them dismantle the house for firewood.

sentences.zh: 所居室唯有一鹿床，竹樹環繞。

translations.literal: The room he lived in held only a deer-hide couch, ringed by bamboo and trees.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a room with only a deer-hide couch, surrounded by bamboo and trees.

sentences.zh: 天監初，御史中丞任昉尋其兄履之，欲造而不敢，望而歎曰：「其室雖邇，其人甚遠。

translations.literal: Early in Tianjian, Imperial Censor Ren Fang sought his elder brother Lüzhi and wished to visit but did not dare; gazing from afar he sighed, "The house is near, yet the man is far."
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian, censor Ren Fang sought his brother Lüzhi, wanting to visit yet afraid; he sighed from afar, "Near the house, far the man."

sentences.zh: 」爲名流所欽尚如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he honored by the famous.
translations.idiomatic: So the famous honored him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與吳郡范元琰俱徵，並不到。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he and Fan Yuanyan of Wu commandery were both summoned, and neither came.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he and Fan Yuanyan of Wu were summoned together; neither came.

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁峻謂之曰：「往者，天地閉，賢人隱；

translations.literal: Yuan Jun of Chen commandery said to him, "Formerly, when Heaven and Earth were shut, worthies hid;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jun of Chen said to him, "Once Heaven and Earth were closed and worthies hid;

sentences.zh: 今世路已清，而子猶遁，可乎？

translations.literal: today the age's road is clear—yet you still withdraw. Is that fitting?"
translations.idiomatic: now the way is open—yet you still flee. How can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔周德雖興，夷、齊不厭薇蕨；

translations.literal: He answered, "Of old, though Zhou virtue was rising, Boyi and Shuqi did not weary of fern and bracken;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Though Zhou's virtue was rising, Boyi and Shuqi still lived on ferns;

sentences.zh: 漢道方盛，黃、綺無悶山林。

translations.literal: when Han's way was at its height, Huang and Qi were not troubled in mountain and forest.
translations.idiomatic: when Han flourished, Huang and Qi were untroubled in the hills."

sentences.zh: 爲仁由己，何關人世！

translations.literal: To practice benevolence lies with oneself—what has it to do with the world of men!"
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence is one's own affair—what has it to do with the age!"

sentences.zh: 況僕非往賢之類邪？」

translations.literal: Besides, am I of the sort of those worthies of old?"
translations.idiomatic: And am I their kind of man?"

sentences.zh: 後於鐘山聽講，母王氏忽有疾，兄弟欲召之。

translations.literal: Later, while listening to lectures on Zhongshan, his mother Lady Wang suddenly fell ill; his brothers wished to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, lecturing on Zhongshan, he heard his mother was ill; his brothers meant to call him home.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「孝緒至性冥通，必當自到。

translations.literal: His mother said, "Xiaoxu's nature is utmost filial and joins with the unseen—he will surely come of himself."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "Xiaoxu's filial nature pierces the unseen—he will come on his own."

sentences.zh: 」果心驚而返，鄰里嗟異之。

translations.literal: Sure enough his heart leapt and he returned; neighbors sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: His heart indeed started and he returned; neighbors marveled.

sentences.zh: 合藥須得生人參，舊傳鐘山所出，孝緒躬歷幽險，累日不值。

translations.literal: To compound medicine they needed fresh ginseng; tradition said it grew on Zhongshan, and Xiaoxu himself traversed dangerous ravines for many days without finding any.
translations.idiomatic: The prescription needed fresh ginseng, said to grow on Zhongshan; he searched the wild ravines for days without success.

sentences.zh: 忽見一鹿前行，孝緒感而隨後，至一所遂滅，就視，果獲此草。

translations.literal: Suddenly he saw a deer go ahead; moved, he followed, and where it vanished he looked and indeed found the herb.
translations.idiomatic: A deer appeared; he followed it in wonder, and where it vanished he found the plant.

sentences.zh: 母得服之，遂愈。

translations.literal: His mother took it and was cured.
translations.idiomatic: His mother took it and recovered.

sentences.zh: 時皆歎其孝感所致。

translations.literal: All then praised this as the fruit of filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: All said filial feeling had wrought it.

sentences.zh: 時有善筮者張有道謂孝緒曰：「見子隱跡而心難明，自非考之龜蓍，無以驗也。

translations.literal: At the time the skilled diviner Zhang Youdao said to Xiaoxu, "I see you hide your tracks yet your heart is hard to read; unless we test by tortoise and yarrow, there is no proof."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Zhang Youdao told him, "You hide your tracks and your heart is obscure; only tortoise and yarrow can test you."

sentences.zh: 」及布卦，旣揲五爻，曰：「此將爲《咸》，應感之法，非嘉遁之兆。

translations.literal: When the hexagram was cast and five lines had been counted, he said, "This will become *Influence*—the hexagram of responsive feeling, not an omen of noble withdrawal."
translations.idiomatic: Casting the lines, he stopped at five and said, "This becomes *Influence*—responsive feeling, not noble retreat."

sentences.zh: 」孝緒曰：「安知後爻不爲上九？

translations.literal: Xiaoxu said, "How do you know the next line will not be the top nine?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxu said, "Who says the next line is not top nine?"

sentences.zh: 」果成《遁卦》。

translations.literal: It indeed became the hexagram *Retreat*.
translations.idiomatic: It became *Retreat*.

sentences.zh: 有道歎曰：「此謂『肥遁無不利。

translations.literal: Youdao sighed and said, "This is 'Fat retreat—nothing unfavorable.'"
translations.idiomatic: Youdao sighed, "This is 'Fat retreat—nothing unfavorable.'"

sentences.zh: 』象實應德，心迹幷也。

translations.literal: " The image truly answers to virtue; heart and track are one."
translations.idiomatic: " Image and virtue match; heart and trail are one."

sentences.zh: 」孝緒曰：「雖獲《遁卦》，而上九爻不發，升遐之道，便當高謝許生。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu said, "Though I receive *Retreat*, the top nine line does not stir—the way of ascending afar must soon make me take leave of Master Xu's sort."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxu said, "Though I get *Retreat*, top nine never stirs—the high path of withdrawal will soon make me quit Xu You's company."

sentences.zh: 」乃著《高隱傳》，上自炎、黃，終於天監之末，斟酌分爲三品，凡若干卷。

translations.literal: He then wrote the *Record of High Reclusion*, from the Flame and Yellow emperors down to the end of Tianjian, weighing and dividing them into three grades, altogether several tens of scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the *Record of High Reclusion* from Yan and Huang to Tianjian's end, sorted into three grades in several tens of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又著論云：「夫至道之本，貴在無爲；

translations.literal: He also wrote a treatise saying, "The root of the utmost Way lies in nonaction;
translations.idiomatic: He argued in a treatise: "The utmost Way's root is nonaction;

sentences.zh: 聖人之跡，存乎拯弊。

translations.literal: the traces of the sage remain in rescuing what is broken.
translations.idiomatic: the sage's traces remain in rescuing decay."

sentences.zh: 弊拯由跡，跡用有乖於本，本旣無爲，爲非道之至。

translations.literal: When decay is rescued by traces, the use of traces conflicts with the root; since the root is nonaction, action is not the fullness of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Rescuing decay needs traces, yet traces war with the root; the root is nonaction, so action is not the Way's fullness.

sentences.zh: 然不垂其跡，則世無以平；

translations.literal: Yet if traces are not let fall, the world has no means to be set level;
translations.idiomatic: Yet without traces the world cannot be leveled;

sentences.zh: 不究其本，則道實交喪。

translations.literal: if the root is not pursued, the Way in truth is lost in crossing.
translations.idiomatic: without pursuing the root, the Way itself is lost in the crossing."

sentences.zh: 丘、旦將存其跡，故宜權晦其本；

translations.literal: Confucius and the Duke of Zhou wished to preserve their traces, and so should for a time hide their root;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and the Duke of Zhou kept their traces and rightly veiled their root for a time;

sentences.zh: 老、莊但明其本，亦宜深抑其跡。

translations.literal: Laozi and Zhuangzi only clarified their root, and so should deeply restrain their traces.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi and Zhuangzi clarified the root and rightly pressed their traces down."

sentences.zh: 跡旣可抑，數子所以有餘；

translations.literal: Since traces can be restrained, those several masters therefore have surplus;
translations.idiomatic: Traces can be restrained, so those masters have something left over;

sentences.zh: 本方見晦，尼丘是故不足。

translations.literal: since the root was hidden, Confucius therefore falls short.
translations.idiomatic: the root was hidden, so Confucius falls short."

sentences.zh: 非得一之士，闕彼明智；

translations.literal: Those who attain only one side lack that bright wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: Men of one side lack that bright wisdom;

sentences.zh: 體二之徒，獨懷鑒識。

translations.literal: those who embody both alone hold the mirror of discernment.
translations.idiomatic: those who hold both carry the mirror of insight."

sentences.zh: 然聖已極照，反創其跡；

translations.literal: Yet the sage had already reached utmost illumination and in turn created his traces;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage, already utmost in light, still made traces;

sentences.zh: 賢未居宗，更言其本。

translations.literal: the worthy had not yet taken the chief seat and again spoke of the root.
translations.idiomatic: the worthy, not yet chief, again spoke of the root."

sentences.zh: 良由跡須拯世，非聖不能；

translations.literal: Truly because traces must rescue the age, it is not for any but a sage;
translations.idiomatic: Traces must save the age—only a sage can;

sentences.zh: 本實明理，在賢可照。

translations.literal: the root in truth clarifies principle, and in the worthy it can shine.
translations.idiomatic: the root clarifies principle—in the worthy it can shine."

sentences.zh: 若能體茲本跡，悟彼抑揚，則孔、莊之意，其過半矣。」

translations.literal: If one can embody this root and these traces and awaken to that restraint and that display, then the intent of Confucius and Zhuangzi is more than half grasped."
translations.idiomatic: Grasp root and trace, their restraint and display, and you hold more than half of Confucius and Zhuangzi."

sentences.zh: 南平元襄王聞其名，致書要之，不赴。

translations.literal: Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping heard his name and sent a letter summoning him; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuanxiang of Nanping summoned him by letter; he would not go.

sentences.zh: 孝緒曰：「非志驕富貴，但性畏廟堂。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu said, "It is not that my will is proud of wealth and rank, but that my nature fears the temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I do not scorn wealth, but I fear the court.

sentences.zh: 若使麏䴥可驂，何以異夫驥騄。」

translations.literal: If deer and roebuck could draw the chariot, how would that differ from matchless steeds?"
translations.idiomatic: If deer and roebuck could be harnessed, how would that differ from thoroughbreds?"

sentences.zh: 初，建武末，青溪宮東門無故自崩，大風拔東宮門外楊樹。

translations.literal: Early on, at the end of Jianwu, the east gate of Qingxi Palace collapsed for no reason, and a great wind uprooted the poplars outside the Eastern Palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Late Jianwu, Qingxi Palace's east gate fell without cause, and a great wind uprooted the Eastern Palace poplars.

sentences.zh: 或以問孝緒，孝緒曰：「青溪皇家舊宅。

translations.literal: Some asked Xiaoxu about it; Xiaoxu said, "Qingxi is the royal house's old dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about it, Xiaoxu said, "Qingxi was the imperial clan's old seat.

sentences.zh: 齊爲木行，東者木位，今東門自壞，木其衰矣。」

translations.literal: Qi belonged to the Wood phase; east is Wood's position—now the east gate has collapsed of itself: Wood is failing."
translations.idiomatic: Qi ruled by Wood; east is Wood's place—the east gate fell by itself: Wood is failing."

sentences.zh: 鄱陽忠烈王妃，孝緒之姊。
