translations.literal: The princess-consort of Poyang, loyal and fierce, was Xiaoxu's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister was princess-consort of Poyang, styled loyal and fierce.

sentences.zh: 王嘗命駕，欲就之遊，孝緒鑿垣而逃，卒不肯見。

translations.literal: The prince once ordered his carriage, wishing to visit and keep his company; Xiaoxu broke through the wall and fled, and in the end would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once drove out to visit him; Xiaoxu broke through the wall and fled, and never would meet him.

sentences.zh: 諸甥歲時饋遺，一無所納。

translations.literal: When nephews brought yearly gifts, he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Nephews' yearly gifts he refused entirely.

sentences.zh: 人或怪之，答云：「非我始願，故不受也。」

translations.literal: Some thought it strange; he answered, "It was never my first wish, and so I do not receive."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "It was never what I first wished for, so I will not take it."

sentences.zh: 其恒所供養石像，先有損壞，心欲治補，經一夜忽然完復，衆並異之。

translations.literal: The stone image he always made offering to had earlier been damaged; he wished to repair it, and after one night it was suddenly whole again—all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: A stone image he worshipped had been damaged; he meant to mend it, and overnight it was whole—everyone marveled.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Datong, at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 門徒誄其德行，諡曰文貞處士。

translations.literal: His disciples eulogized his virtue and conduct; his posthumous title was Recluse Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples praised his conduct; he was titled Recluse Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 所著《七錄》等書二百五十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: His works such as the *Bibliographic Treatise in Seven Categories*, two hundred fifty scrolls in all, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Works including the *Sevenfold Bibliography*, 250 scrolls in all, circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 陶弘景

translations.literal: Tao Hongjing
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hongjing

sentences.zh: 陶弘景字通明，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Tao Hongjing, styled Tongming, was a man of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hongjing, styled Tongming, came from Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初，母夢青龍自懷而出，幷見兩天人手執香爐來至其所，已而有娠，遂產弘景。

translations.literal: At first his mother dreamed a green dragon came forth from her womb, and she also saw two heaven-men bearing censers come to her place; afterward she conceived and bore Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed a green dragon left her womb and two celestial men with censers came to her; then she bore Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 幼有異操。

translations.literal: In childhood he had an uncommon bent.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was unlike others.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，得葛洪《神仙傳》，晝夜研尋，便有養生之志。

translations.literal: At ten he obtained Ge Hong's *Biographies of Immortals* and studied it day and night, and then had the will to nurture life.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he found Ge Hong's *Biographies of Immortals*, studied it day and night, and resolved to seek long life.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「仰青雲，睹白日，不覺爲遠矣。

translations.literal: He told others, "Looking up at blue clouds and gazing at the white sun, I do not feel them far away."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Raise your eyes to blue clouds and the white sun—they do not seem far."

sentences.zh: 」及長，身長七尺四寸，神儀明秀，朗目疏眉，細形長耳。

translations.literal: When grown he stood seven feet four inches; his spirit and bearing were bright and elegant, his eyes clear and brows sparse, his form slender and ears long.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he stood seven feet four; bright of spirit, clear-eyed, sparse-browed, slender, long-eared.

sentences.zh: 讀書萬餘卷。

translations.literal: He read more than ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He read over ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 善琴棊，工草隸。

translations.literal: He was skilled at zither and chess and accomplished in draft and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He played zither and chess and wrote draft and clerical script well.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，齊高帝作相，引爲諸王侍讀，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: Before he had capped his years, when Qi Gaodi was prime minister, he was brought in as lecturer to the princes and appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping year, with Qi Gaodi as prime minister, he became princes' lecturer and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 雖在朱門，閉影不交外物，唯以披閱爲務。

translations.literal: Though he was in the vermilion gate, he shut his shadow away and mingled with nothing outside, taking only reading as his task.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived in the great house, he hid from the world and read without cease.

sentences.zh: 朝儀故事，多取決焉。

translations.literal: Court ritual and precedent mostly took their decisions from him.
translations.idiomatic: Court ritual mostly followed his judgment.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，上表辭祿，詔許之，賜以束帛。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming he submitted a memorial resigning his salary; the emperor approved and granted him silks.
translations.idiomatic: Yongming year ten he memorialized to resign his stipend; the emperor agreed and gave him silks.

sentences.zh: 及發，公卿祖之於征虜亭，供帳甚盛，車馬填咽，咸云宋、齊以來，未有斯事。

translations.literal: When he set out, the court nobles saw him off at the Pacifying-the-Barbarians Pavilion; the feast was very grand, carriages and horses jammed the road—all said that since Song and Qi there had never been such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: At his departure nobles feasted him at the Pacifying-the-Barbarians Pavilion—carriages choked the road; none since Song and Qi had seen the like.

sentences.zh: 朝野榮之。

translations.literal: Court and countryside honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country honored him.

sentences.zh: 於是止于句容之句曲山。

translations.literal: He then stopped on Mt Gouqu in Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: He settled on Mt Gouqu in Jurong.

sentences.zh: 恒曰：「此山下是第八洞宮，名金壇華陽之天，周回一百五十里。

translations.literal: He constantly said, "Below this mountain is the eighth grotto-palace, called the Golden Altar Huayang Heaven, circling one hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: He always said, "Below this mountain lies the eighth grotto-palace—the Golden Altar Huayang Heaven, one hundred fifty li around.

sentences.zh: 昔漢有咸陽三茅君得道，來掌此山，故謂之茅山。

translations.literal: In Han times the Three Lord Mao of Xianyang attained the Way and came to govern this mountain; hence it was called Mt Mao.
translations.idiomatic: In Han the Three Mao lords of Xianyang attained the Way and ruled this mountain—hence Mt Mao.

sentences.zh: 」乃中山立館，自號華陽隱居。

translations.literal: " He then built a lodge on Mt Zhong and styled himself the Recluse of Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: " He built a lodge on Mt Zhong and called himself the Recluse of Huayang.

sentences.zh: 始從東陽孫游岳受符圖經法。

translations.literal: At first he received talisman charts and classic methods from Sun Yoyue of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: First he studied talismans and charts under Sun Yoyue of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 遍歷名山，尋訪仙藥。

translations.literal: He traveled every famous mountain seeking elixirs.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged famous mountains seeking elixirs.

sentences.zh: 每經澗谷，必坐臥其間，吟詠盤桓，不能已已。

translations.literal: Whenever he passed a ravine he would sit or lie within it, chanting and lingering, unable to tear himself away.
translations.idiomatic: At every ravine he sat or lay, chanting and lingering, unable to leave.

sentences.zh: 時沈約爲東陽郡守，高其志節，累書要之，不至。

translations.literal: Shen Yue was then prefect of Dongyang; he honored Hongjing's integrity, wrote repeatedly to summon him, but he never came.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, Dongyang prefect, prized his integrity and wrote again and again; Hongjing never came.

sentences.zh: 弘景爲人，圓通謙謹，出處冥會，心如明鏡，遇物便了，言無煩舛，有亦輒覺。

translations.literal: Hongjing was rounded, tactful, and modest; his comings and goings matched deep design; his mind was like a bright mirror—he grasped things at once, his words never tangled, and he sensed error the moment it appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Rounded and modest, he matched occasion in silence; his mind was a mirror—things cleared at a glance, speech never snarled, fault felt at once.

sentences.zh: 建武中，齊宜都王鏗爲明帝所害，其夜，弘景夢鏗告別，因訪其幽冥中事，多說秘異，因著《夢記》焉。

translations.literal: During Jianwu Prince Keng of Yidu was killed by Mingdi; that night Hongjing dreamed Keng taking leave; he inquired into affairs of the nether world, heard many secret marvels, and wrote Dream Records.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu Prince Keng of Yidu died by Mingdi's hand; that night Hongjing dreamed him farewell, asked of the shades, heard strange secrets, and wrote Dream Records.

sentences.zh: 永元初，更築三層樓，弘景處其上，弟子居其中，賓客至其下，與物遂絕，唯一家僮得侍其旁。

translations.literal: Early Yongyuan he built a three-story tower: Hongjing lived on top, disciples in the middle, guests below—cut off from the world; only one houseboy waited beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongyuan he raised a three-story tower—Hongjing above, disciples between, guests below—world cut off; one boy alone served at his side.

sentences.zh: 特愛松風，每聞其響，欣然爲樂。

translations.literal: He especially loved pine wind; whenever he heard it he took joy in it.
translations.idiomatic: He loved pine wind; at its sound he always rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 有時獨游泉石，望見者以爲仙人。

translations.literal: Sometimes he wandered alone among springs and rocks; those who saw him took him for an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he roamed springs and stone alone; watchers thought him an immortal.

sentences.zh: 性好著述，尚奇異，顧惜光景，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: By nature he loved writing and prized the strange; he cherished time, and in old age grew only more intense.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to write and prized the strange, hoarded daylight, and in old age grew keener still.

sentences.zh: 尤明陰陽五行，風角星算，山川地理，方圖產物，醫術本草。

translations.literal: He was especially versed in yin-yang and the five phases, wind angles and star reckoning, mountains and rivers, local products on maps, medicine and materia medica.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at yin-yang and five phases, wind and stars, land and maps, drugs and herbs.

sentences.zh: 著《帝代年曆》，又嘗造渾天象，云「修道所須，非止史官是用」。

translations.literal: He wrote Imperial Eras Chronology and once made an armillary heaven model, saying, "What cultivating the Way requires is not merely for historiographers."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Imperial Eras Chronology and once built an armillary sphere, saying cultivation needs more than historians use.

sentences.zh: 義師平建康，聞議禪代，弘景援引圖讖，數處皆成「梁」字，令弟子進之。

translations.literal: When the army of righteousness took Jiankang and talk of transfer of the mandate arose, Hongjing drew on prognostic texts—several places formed the character Liang—and had disciples present them.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army took Jiankang and abdication was debated, Hongjing cited omens where Liang formed again and again and sent disciples to present them.

sentences.zh: 高祖旣早與之遊，及卽位後，恩禮逾篤，書問不絕，冠蓋相望。

translations.literal: Gaozu had long been his friend; after enthronement favor deepened, letters unceasing, emissaries in constant view.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had known him early; enthroned, his grace deepened—letters without end, coaches in sight.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，移居積金東澗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian he moved to Golden Accumulation's eastern brook.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year four he moved to Golden Accumulation's eastern stream.

sentences.zh: 善辟穀導引之法，年逾八十而有壯容。

translations.literal: Skilled in grain avoidance and guiding exercises; past eighty he still looked robust.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in fasting and breath guidance; past eighty he still looked hale.

sentences.zh: 深慕張良之爲人，云「古賢莫比」。

translations.literal: He deeply admired Zhang Liang, saying no ancient worthy could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply admired Zhang Liang, saying no sage of old could equal him.

sentences.zh: 曾夢佛授其菩提記，名爲勝力菩薩。

translations.literal: Once he dreamed the Buddha gave him a bodhi record, naming him the Bodhisattva Victorious Power.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed the Buddha gave him a bodhi record and named him the Bodhisattva Victorious Power.

sentences.zh: 乃詣鄮縣阿育王塔自誓，受五大戒。

translations.literal: He went to King Asoka's tower in Mao county, vowed himself, and received the five great precepts.
translations.idiomatic: He went to King Asoka's stupa in Mao, vowed, and took the five great precepts.

sentences.zh: 後太宗臨南徐州，欽其風素，召至後堂，與談論數日而去，太宗甚敬異之。

translations.literal: Later Taizong governed southern Xuzhou, honored his integrity, summoned him to the rear hall, talked for days and sent him away—Taizong greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizong held southern Xuzhou, prized his character, called him to the rear hall, talked days, and sent him off in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 大通初，令獻二刀於高祖，其一名善勝，一名成勝，竝爲佳寶。

translations.literal: Early Datong he sent two blades to Gaozu—one named Good Victory, one Achieved Victory—both fine treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Early Datong he presented two swords to Gaozu—Good Victory and Achieved Victory—both prized blades.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，卒，時年八十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died, aged eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Datong year two he died, at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 顏色不變，屈申如恒。

translations.literal: His color did not change; his limbs flexed as before.
translations.idiomatic: His color held; his limbs moved as ever.

sentences.zh: 詔贈中散大夫，諡曰貞白先生，仍遣舍人監護喪事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and honored as Master Zhenbai, with a household steward to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The court made him palace attendant posthumously, titled Master Zhenbai, and sent a steward to oversee the rites.

sentences.zh: 弘景遺令薄葬，弟子遵而行之。

translations.literal: Hongjing left orders for a modest burial, which his disciples followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing ordered a plain burial; disciples obeyed.

sentences.zh: 諸葛璩

translations.literal: Zhuge Ju
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ju

sentences.zh: 諸葛璩字幼玟，琅邪陽都人，世居京口。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ju, styled Youmin, was a man of Yangdu in Langye; his family had long lived at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ju, styled Youmin, came from Yangdu in Langye; his clan had long dwelt at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 璩幼事徵士關康之，博涉經史。

translations.literal: As a youth Ju studied under the recluse Guan Kangzhi and ranged widely through classics and history.
translations.idiomatic: Ju as a boy served the recluse Guan Kangzhi and ranged classics and history.

sentences.zh: 復師徵士臧榮緒。

translations.literal: He also studied under the recluse Zang Rongxu.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied under the recluse Zang Rongxu.

sentences.zh: 榮緒著《晉書》，稱璩有發擿之功，方之壺遂。

translations.literal: When Rongxu wrote the Jin history he praised Ju's contributions to discovery, comparing him to Hu Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxu's Jin history credits Ju with uncovering sources and compares him to Hu Sui.

sentences.zh: 齊建武初，南徐州行事江祀薦璩於明帝曰：「璩安貧守道，悅《禮》敦《詩》，未嘗投刺邦宰，曳裾府寺，如其簡退，可以揚清厲俗。

translations.literal: Early in Jianwu Jiang Si, acting for southern Xuzhou, recommended Ju to Mingdi: "Ju keeps to poverty and the Way, delights in the Rites and honors the Odes, never calls on a prefect or trails his robe through offices—with such simplicity he could purify custom. I ask he be made aide in the advisory staff."
translations.idiomatic: Early Jianwu Jiang Si of southern Xuzhou told Mingdi: "Ju keeps poverty and the Way, loves Rites and Odes, never visits a magistrate or haunts offices—such withdrawal could purify custom. Make him advisory aide."

sentences.zh: 請辟爲議曹從事。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed; Ju declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented; Ju refused and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 」帝許之，璩辭不去。

translations.literal: Xie Tiao of Chen commandery, as prefect of Donghai, issued an edict: "Long ago Sun Qiu of the east bound his sash and lowered the banner of Dragon Hill;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao of Chen, Donghai prefect, wrote: "Once Sun Qiu bound his sash and lowered Dragon Hill's banner;

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝朓爲東海太守，教曰：「昔長孫東組，降龍丘之節；

translations.literal: Kong Wenju drove north with light carts and won the name of lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wenju drove north in light carts and won fame for lofty virtue.

sentences.zh: 文舉北輜，高通德之稱。

translations.literal: Thus they stirred the greedy and stiffened the timid, setting the pattern of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: So they stirred the greedy and stiffened the timid, setting conduct for others.

sentences.zh: 所以激貪立懦，式揚風範。

translations.literal: The gentleman Zhuge Ju, touched by lofty winds, follows the wheel-tracks of earlier worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Recluse Zhuge Ju, touched by lofty winds, follows earlier worthies' tracks.

sentences.zh: 處士諸葛璩，高風所漸，結轍前脩。

translations.literal: Does he hide a pearl in coarse cloth, jade in his breast, waiting for price?
translations.idiomatic: Does he hide pearl in sackcloth, jade in his breast, waiting for price?

sentences.zh: 豈懷珠披褐，韜玉待價？

translations.literal: Or does he go alone in hidden integrity, serving no prince?
translations.idiomatic: Or does he walk alone in hidden integrity, serving no lord?

sentences.zh: 將幽貞獨往，不事王侯者邪？

translations.literal: I hear that in serving his mother he is poor as bean-broth, and in supporting her lacks even steamed greens—how can he alone enjoy ten thousand bushels and forget these five pecks?
translations.idiomatic: I hear he serves his mother on bean broth and can barely feed her greens—how enjoy ten thousand bushels and forget five pecks?

sentences.zh: 聞事親有啜菽之窶，就養寡藜蒸之給，豈得獨享萬鐘，而忘茲五秉？

translations.literal: Let him be given a hundred bushels of grain."
translations.idiomatic: Grant him a hundred bushels of grain."

sentences.zh: 可餉穀百斛。

translations.literal: " During Tianjian Prefect Xiao Chen, Inspector An Cheng Prince Xiu, and Prince of Poyang Hui all honored him distinctly.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Tianjian Prefect Xiao Chen, Inspector Prince Xiu of An Cheng, and Prince Hui of Poyang all treated him with special honor.

sentences.zh: 」天監中，太守蕭琛、刺史安成王秀、鄱陽王恢並禮異焉。

translations.literal: Ju mourned his mother to emaciation; Hui repeatedly sent inquiries of care.
translations.idiomatic: Ju wasted away in mourning his mother; Hui wrote again and again to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 璩丁母憂毀瘠，恢累加存問。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was nominated as cultivated talent but would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning done, he was nominated cultivated talent and refused.

sentences.zh: 服闋，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: Ju was diligent in teaching; students came daily, but his house was narrow and could not hold them, so Prefect Zhang You built a lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ju taught tirelessly; students came daily until his house would not hold them, and Prefect Zhang You built a lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 璩性勤於誨誘，後生就學者日至，居宅狹陋，無以容之，太守張友爲起講舍。

translations.literal: Ju kept himself pure and upright; wife and children never saw pleasure or anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was pure in conduct; wife and children never saw joy or anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 璩處身清正，妻子不見喜慍之色。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he labored without cease in lecture and recitation, and people honored him all the more for it.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and night he lectured without pause, and the world honored him the more.

sentences.zh: 旦夕孜孜，講誦不輟，時人益以此宗之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Gaozu ordered the prefect Wang Fen questioned; Fen answered fully as things were, but before Ju could be summoned he died at home that year.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven Gaozu asked Prefect Wang Fen, who told the truth; before Ju could be called he died at home that year.

sentences.zh: 七年，高祖敕問太守王份，份卽具以實對，未及徵用，是年卒於家。

translations.literal: Ju's writings filled twenty scrolls; his disciple Liu Xiao collected and recorded them.
translations.idiomatic: His writings ran twenty scrolls; disciple Liu Xiao compiled them.

sentences.zh: 璩所著文章二十卷，門人劉曒集而錄之。

translations.literal: Shen Yan
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yan

sentences.zh: 沈顗字處默，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yan, styled Chumo, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yan, styled Chumo, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父坦之，齊都官郎。

translations.literal: His father Tanzhi was director of the Ministry of Justice under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanzhi was Qi director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 顗幼清靜有至行，慕黃叔度、徐孺子之爲人。

translations.literal: As a boy Yan was quiet and possessed utmost conduct; he admired Huang Shidu and Xu Jizi.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quiet and of utmost conduct, admiring Huang Shidu and Xu Jizi.

sentences.zh: 讀書不爲章句，著述不尚浮華。

translations.literal: In reading he did not chase glosses; in writing he did not pursue ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He read without chasing glosses and wrote without chasing ornament.

sentences.zh: 常獨處一室，人罕見其面。

translations.literal: He often sat alone in one room; few saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: He often sat alone in one room; few ever saw his face.

sentences.zh: 顗從叔勃，貴顯齊世，每還吳興，賓客填咽，顗不至其門。

translations.literal: Yan's paternal uncle Bo rose to glory in Qi; whenever he returned to Wuxing guests filled the courtyard, but Yan never came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Bo was grand in Qi; when Bo returned to Wuxing guests choked the court, but Yan never came to his gate.

sentences.zh: 勃就之，顗送迎不越於閫。

translations.literal: Bo went to him; Yan's coming and going never crossed the threshold.
translations.idiomatic: Bo visited him; Yan's courtesy never crossed the threshold.

sentences.zh: 勃歎息曰：「吾乃今知貴不如賤。」

translations.literal: Bo sighed and said, "Only today do I know that noble rank is not as good as low."
translations.idiomatic: Bo sighed: "Only now I know rank is worse than low estate."

sentences.zh: 俄徵爲南郡王左常侍，不就。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as left regular attendant to the Prince of Nan commandery but would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned as left attendant to the Prince of Nan—he refused.

sentences.zh: 顗內行甚脩，事母兄弟孝友，爲鄉里所稱慕。

translations.literal: Yan's inner conduct was very strict; in serving mother and brothers he was filial and friendly, and the district praised and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: His inner life was strict; filial to mother, friendly to brothers—the district praised him.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，徵著作郎；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he was summoned as drafting secretary;
translations.idiomatic: Yongming year three he was called drafting secretary;

sentences.zh: 建武二年，徵太子舍人，俱不赴。

translations.literal: in the second year of Jianwu as crown prince attendant—he went to neither.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu year two as crown prince attendant—he went to neither.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，又徵通直郎，亦不赴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was again summoned as courier gentleman and again would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan year two he was called courier gentleman and again refused.

sentences.zh: 顗素不治家產，值齊末兵荒，與家人幷日而食。

translations.literal: Yan never managed family property; at the end of Qi, with soldiers and famine, he and his household ate one meal a day.
translations.idiomatic: He never kept house; at Qi's end, war and famine, his household ate once a day.

sentences.zh: 或有饋其梁肉者，閉門不受。

translations.literal: When someone offered him grain and meat he shut the door and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Offered grain and meat, he shut the door and would not take it.

sentences.zh: 唯以樵采自資，怡怡然恒不改其樂。

translations.literal: He supported himself only by gathering firewood, yet remained easy and never lost his joy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by firewood alone, yet stayed easy and never lost his joy.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，大舉北伐，訂民丁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian a great northern campaign was launched and commoners were levied.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year four a great northern campaign levied the people.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守柳惲以顗從役，揚州別駕陸任以書責之，惲大慚，厚禮而遣之。

translations.literal: Wuxing Prefect Liu Yun wanted Yan for corvee; the vice-prefect of Yangzhou Lu Ren wrote to rebuke him, and Yun was deeply ashamed, treated him with great courtesy, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Liu Yun pressed Yan into corvee; Yangzhou vice-prefect Lu Ren rebuked him in writing; Yun was ashamed, honored him, and released him.

sentences.zh: 其年卒於家。

translations.literal: That year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 所著文章數十篇。

translations.literal: His writings ran to several dozen pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His writings ran to several dozen pieces.

sentences.zh: 劉慧斐

translations.literal: Liu Huifei
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huifei

sentences.zh: 劉慧斐字文宣，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Huifei, styled Wensuan, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huifei, styled Wensuan, came from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 少博學，能屬文，起家安成王法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he was broadly learned and could write; he began office as aide in the law bureau of the Prince of An Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Young, broadly learned and able to write, he began as law-bureau aide to the Prince of An Cheng.

sentences.zh: 嘗還都，途經尋陽，游於匡山，過處士張孝秀，相得甚歡，遂有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Once returning to the capital he passed Xunyang, wandered Mt Kuang, met the recluse Zhang Xiaoxiu, and took great delight in him; he then resolved to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court he passed Xunyang, roamed Mt Kuang, met recluse Zhang Xiaoxiu, delighted in him, and resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 因不仕，居於東林寺。

translations.literal: He therefore left office and lived at East Grove Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He left office and dwelt at East Grove Temple.

sentences.zh: 又於山北構園一所，號曰離垢園，時人乃謂爲離垢先生。

translations.literal: He also built a garden north of the mountain called the Garden Free of Defilement; people then called him Master Free of Defilement.
translations.idiomatic: North of the mountain he built the Garden Free of Defilement; men called him Master Free of Defilement.

sentences.zh: 慧斐尤明釋典，工篆隸，在山手寫佛經二千餘卷，常所誦者百餘卷。

translations.literal: Huifei was especially versed in Buddhist canon and skilled in seal and clerical script; on the mountain he copied more than two thousand scrolls of sutras by hand and regularly recited over a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in Buddhist canon and seal script, copied two thousand sutra scrolls by hand on the mountain, and daily recited over a hundred.

sentences.zh: 晝夜行道，孜孜不怠，遠近欽慕之。

translations.literal: Day and night he practiced the Way without slackening; near and far admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night he walked the Way without slackening; near and far admired him.

sentences.zh: 太宗臨江州，遺以几杖。

translations.literal: Taizong governed Jiang province and sent him a couch and staff.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong governing Jiang sent him couch and staff.

sentences.zh: 論者云：自遠法師沒後，將二百年，始有張、劉之盛矣。

translations.literal: Critics said that from Master Yuan's death it had been nearly two hundred years before Zhang and Liu flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said nearly two hundred years after Master Yuan died before Zhang and Liu rose again.

sentences.zh: 世祖及武陵王等書問不絕。

translations.literal: Shizu and the Prince of Wuling and others wrote without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu and the Prince of Wuling wrote without cease.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Datong year two he died, at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 范元琰

translations.literal: Fan Yuanyan
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuanyan

sentences.zh: 范元琰字伯珪，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Fan Yuanyan, styled Bogui, was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yuanyan, styled Bogui, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖悅之，太學博士徵，不至。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuezhi was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy but would not go.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuezhi was summoned imperial erudite and would not go.

sentences.zh: 父靈瑜，居父憂，以毀卒。

translations.literal: His father Lingyu died in mourning for his father, wasted by grief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingyu died mourning his father, destroyed by grief.

sentences.zh: 元琰時童孺，哀慕盡禮，親黨異之。

translations.literal: Yuanyan was then a child; his mourning and yearning fulfilled every rite, and kin marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan was still a child; his mourning fulfilled every rite, and kin marveled.

sentences.zh: 及長好學，博通經史，兼精佛義。

translations.literal: Grown, he loved learning, ranged through classics and history, and was also versed in Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he loved learning, ranged classics and history, and knew Buddhist teaching.

sentences.zh: 然性謙敬，不以所長驕人。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was modest and did not flaunt what he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Yet modest by nature, he never flaunted what he knew.

sentences.zh: 家貧，唯以園蔬爲業。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he lived only by garden vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he lived only on garden vegetables.

sentences.zh: 嘗出行，見人盜其菜，元琰遽退走，母問其故，具以實答。

translations.literal: Once on a walk he saw someone stealing his vegetables; Yuanyan hurried away. His mother asked why; he told her fully.
translations.idiomatic: Once walking out he saw a man steal his greens; Yuanyan hurried away. His mother asked; he told all.

sentences.zh: 母問盜者爲誰，答曰：「向所以退，畏其愧恥。

translations.literal: His mother asked who the thief was. He answered, "I withdrew because I feared shaming him.
translations.idiomatic: She asked who stole. He said, "I fled lest I shame him.

sentences.zh: 今啓其名，願不泄也。

translations.literal: Now that I name him, I beg you not to reveal it."
translations.idiomatic: Now I name him—please do not tell."

sentences.zh: 」於是母子秘之。

translations.literal: Mother and son kept the secret.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son kept silence.

sentences.zh: 或有涉溝盜其筍者，元琰因伐木爲橋以渡之。

translations.literal: When someone waded a ditch to steal his bamboo shoots, Yuanyan cut wood and built a bridge for crossing.
translations.idiomatic: When a man waded a ditch to steal bamboo shoots, Yuanyan built a wooden bridge.

sentences.zh: 自是盜者大慚，一鄉無復草竊。

translations.literal: After that the thief was deeply ashamed, and the whole village ceased stealing grass and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Then the thief was ashamed, and the village stopped stealing plants.

sentences.zh: 居常不出城市，獨坐如對嚴賓，見之者莫不改容正色。

translations.literal: He usually did not leave the city; sitting alone he was as if facing stern guests—those who saw him could not but straighten their bearing and color.
translations.idiomatic: He rarely left town; sitting alone as before stern guests, viewers straightened face and bearing.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉瓛深加器異，嘗表稱之。

translations.literal: Liu Huan of Pei greatly prized him and once memorialized in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan of Pei prized him and once memorialized praise.

sentences.zh: 齊建武二年，始徵爲安北參軍事，不赴。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was first summoned as aide to the Army Pacifying the North; he would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu year two he was first summoned aide to the Army Pacifying the North and refused.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，縣令管慧辨上言義行，揚州刺史、臨川王宏辟命，不至。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian the county magistrate Guan Huibian memorialized on his righteous conduct; Yangzhou inspector Prince Linchuan Hong sent a summons—he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year nine the magistrate Guan Huibian praised his conduct; Prince Linchuan of Yangzhou summoned him, and he stayed away.

sentences.zh: 十年，王拜表薦焉，竟未徵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the prince submitted a memorial recommending him; in the end he was never summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Year ten the prince recommended him in a memorial, but no summons ever came.

sentences.zh: 其年卒於家，時年七十。

translations.literal: That year he died at home, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home that year, at seventy.

sentences.zh: 劉訏字彥度，平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xu, courtesy name Yandu, was a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, styled Yandu, came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父靈真，齊武昌太守。

translations.literal: His father Lingzhen was Qi Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingzhen had been Qi administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 訏幼稱純孝，數歲，父母繼卒，訏居喪，哭泣孺慕，幾至滅性，赴吊者莫不傷焉。

translations.literal: From childhood Xu was famed for pure filial piety; when only a few years old his parents died in succession. In mourning he wept with a child's yearning, nearly destroying himself; all who came to condole were moved.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was famed for filial piety; his parents died in turn while he was still small, and his mourning weeping, childlike and desperate, nearly killed him and broke every visitor's heart.

sentences.zh: 後爲伯父所養，事伯母及昆姊，孝友篤至，爲宗族所稱。

translations.literal: Later he was raised by his father's elder brother; toward his uncle's wife and elder sisters his filial affection and brotherly love were so deep that the clan praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle raised him; toward the uncle's wife and his elder sisters he showed such filial love that the clan spoke of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 自傷早孤，人有誤觸其諱者，未嘗不感結流涕。

translations.literal: Grieving his early orphanhood, when anyone carelessly touched a tabooed name he never failed to be overcome and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Still wounded by early orphanhood, he wept whenever someone blundered into a name he could not bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 長兄潔爲之娉妻，剋日成婚，訏聞而逃匿，事息乃還。

translations.literal: His eldest brother Jie secured a wife for him and set the wedding day; Xu heard of it and fled into hiding, returning only when the affair had passed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Jie arranged a bride and fixed the wedding day; Xu fled and hid until the plan collapsed.

sentences.zh: 本州刺史張稷辟爲主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The provincial inspector Zhang Ji summoned him as chief clerk; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial inspector Zhang Ji offered him chief clerk; he refused.

sentences.zh: 主者檄召，訏乃掛檄於樹而逃。

translations.literal: When the authorities issued a summons he hung the document on a tree and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When a summons arrived he nailed it to a tree and ran.

sentences.zh: 訏善玄言，尤精釋典。

translations.literal: Xu was skilled in Dark Learning and especially versed in Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at Dark Learning and knew the Buddhist canon deeply.

sentences.zh: 曾與族兄劉歊聽講於鐘山諸寺，因共卜築宋熙寺東澗，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Once with his clan elder Liu Shao he listened to lectures at monasteries on Mt Zhong, and together they cast lots to build on the east brook of Songxi Monastery, with the will to end their days there.
translations.idiomatic: With his kinsman Liu Shao he heard lectures on Mt Zhong and chose a site east of Songxi Monastery where both meant to live out their lives.

sentences.zh: 天監十七年，卒於歊舍，時年三十一。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianjian he died in Shao's house, aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year seventeen he died in Shao's lodging, at thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 臨終，執歊手曰：「氣絕便斂，斂畢卽埋，靈筵一不須立，勿設饗祀，無求繼嗣。

translations.literal: At the end he took Shao's hand and said: "When breath fails, wrap the body at once; when wrapping is done, bury immediately. Do not set up a spirit altar, do not offer funeral feasts, do not seek heirs."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he gripped Shao's hand: "When I stop breathing, wrap me and bury me—no spirit altar, no funeral feast, no heirs."

sentences.zh: 」歊從而行之。

translations.literal: Shao carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Shao did exactly as he asked.

sentences.zh: 宗人至友相與刊石立銘，諡曰玄貞處士。

translations.literal: Clansmen and close friends together carved stone and set up an inscription; his posthumous title was Recluse of Mysterious Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends raised a stone inscription and gave him the posthumous name Recluse of Mysterious Integrity.

sentences.zh: 劉歊字士光，訏族兄也。

translations.literal: Liu Shao, courtesy name Shiguang, was Xu's clan elder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shao, styled Shiguang, was Xu's elder kinsman.

sentences.zh: 祖乘民，宋冀州刺史；

translations.literal: His grandfather Chenmin was Song Inspector of Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chenmin had been Song inspector of Jizhou;

sentences.zh: 父聞慰，齊正員郎。

translations.literal: his father Wenwei was Qi Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: his father Wenwei, a Qi regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 世爲二千石，皆有清名。

translations.literal: For generations they had held two-thousand-bushel posts, all with a clean name.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had held two-thousand-bushel office, each man leaving a spotless name.

sentences.zh: 歊幼有識慧，四歲喪父，與羣兒同處，獨不戲弄。

translations.literal: Shao from childhood had keen understanding; at four he lost his father. Among the boys he alone would not play.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, he lost his father at four and would not join the other boys at play.

sentences.zh: 六歲誦《論語》、《毛詩》，意所不解，便能問難。

translations.literal: At six he recited the *Analects* and *Mao Odes*; what he did not understand he could at once question.
translations.idiomatic: At six he knew the *Analects* and *Mao Odes* and pressed hard questions on whatever puzzled him.

sentences.zh: 十一，讀《莊子·逍遙篇》，曰：「此可解耳。

translations.literal: At eleven he read the "Free and Easy Wandering" chapter of the *Zhuangzi* and said, "This can be explained."
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he read Zhuangzi's "Free and Easy Wandering" and said, "I can make sense of this."

sentences.zh: 」客因問之，隨問而答，皆有情理，家人每異之。

translations.literal: A guest thereupon questioned him; he answered each question as it came, all with reason—and his family always marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Guests tested him; he answered every question with sense, and his family marveled each time.

sentences.zh: 及長，博學有文才，不娶不仕，與族弟訏並隱居求志，遨遊林澤，以山水書籍相娛而已。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned and had literary talent; he neither married nor took office. With his cousin Xu he recluded to seek his aim, roaming forest and marsh and taking mountains, waters, books, and records for his only pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was learned and literary, never married, never served. With cousin Xu he withdrew to seek his purpose, roaming wild country and finding joy only in landscape and books.

sentences.zh: 常欲避人世，以母老不忍違離，每隨兄霽、杳從宦。

translations.literal: He had long wished to leave the human world, but his mother was old and he could not bear to leave her; he always followed his brothers Ji and Yao in their official rounds.
translations.idiomatic: He yearned to leave the world yet could not abandon his aged mother and so often trailed his brothers Ji and Yao on their posts.

sentences.zh: 少時好施，務周人之急，人或遺之，亦不距也。

translations.literal: In youth he loved to give and strove to relieve others' urgent need; if someone offered him something he never refused.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he loved giving and rushed to ease others' distress; gifts offered him he never turned away.

sentences.zh: 久而歎曰：「受人者必報，不則有愧於人。

translations.literal: After long years he sighed and said, "One who receives from others must repay; otherwise he owes them shame.
translations.idiomatic: In time he sighed: "To receive is to owe; without repayment one lives in debt to others.

sentences.zh: 吾固無以報人，豈可常有愧乎？」

translations.literal: I truly have no way to repay others—how can I always carry such shame?"
translations.idiomatic: I have nothing with which to repay—how can I bear perpetual shame?"

sentences.zh: 天監十七年，無何而著《革終論》。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Tianjian, without warning he composed the *Discourse on Changing the End*.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjian year seventeen he suddenly wrote the *Discourse on Changing the End*.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words run thus:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 死生之事，聖人罕言之矣。

translations.literal: Matters of death and life the sages rarely speak of.
translations.idiomatic: On death and life the sages say little.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「精氣爲物，遊魂爲變，知鬼神之情狀，與天地相似而不違。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "The refined breath becomes things; the wandering soul becomes change—knowing the condition of ghosts and spirits, similar to Heaven and earth yet not opposing them."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Refined breath becomes things, the wandering soul becomes change—to know ghosts and spirits is to be like Heaven and earth and not oppose them."

sentences.zh: 」其言約，其旨妙，其事隱，其意深，未可以臆斷，難得而精核，聊肆狂瞽，請試言之。

translations.literal: His words are spare, his aim subtle, the matter hidden, the meaning deep—not to be cut off by guesswork or finely checked by reckoning; I venture my rash blindness and ask leave to try speech.
translations.idiomatic: The words are few, the aim subtle, the matter hidden, the meaning deep—no guesswork can sever it, no reckoning nail it down; forgive my rashness if I try to speak.

sentences.zh: 夫形慮合而爲生，魂質離而稱死；

translations.literal: Form and thought unite and we call it life; soul-substance separates and we call it death;
translations.idiomatic: Form and thought unite—that is life; soul-substance parts—that is death;

sentences.zh: 合則起動，離則休寂。

translations.literal: united, movement rises; separated, stillness rests.
translations.idiomatic: united, the body stirs; parted, it falls still.

sentences.zh: 當其動也，人皆知其神；

translations.literal: While it moves, all men know its spirit;
translations.idiomatic: While it moves, everyone knows the spirit is there;

sentences.zh: 及其寂也，物莫測其所趣。

translations.literal: when it is still, nothing measures where it tends.
translations.idiomatic: when still, nothing can measure where it goes.

sentences.zh: 皆知則不言而義顯，莫測則逾辯而理微。

translations.literal: What all know needs no words yet meaning shows; what none measures, the more one argues the finer reason grows dim.
translations.idiomatic: What all know needs no words; what none can measure grows dimmer the more one argues.

sentences.zh: 是以勳、華曠而莫陳，姬、孔抑而不說，前達往賢，互生異見。

translations.literal: Therefore the achievements of Xun and Hua lie vast and unspoken; the Ji and Kong line suppressed and did not expound—worthies of old and sages of the past each bore a different view.
translations.idiomatic: So the deeds of Xun and Hua lie vast and unspoken; Ji and Kong held back—and sages of old disagreed.

sentences.zh: 季札云：「骨肉歸於土，魂氣無不之。

translations.literal: Ji Zha said: "Flesh and bone return to earth; breath and soul go everywhere."
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zha said, "Flesh and bone return to earth; breath and soul go everywhere."

sentences.zh: 」莊周云：「生爲徭役，死爲休息。

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou said: "Life is corvée labor; death is rest."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Zhou said, "Life is forced labor; death is rest."

sentences.zh: 」尋此二說，如或相反。

translations.literal: Seek these two sayings—they seem to oppose each other.
translations.idiomatic: Set the two sayings side by side—they seem to contradict.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 氣無不之，神有也；

translations.literal: "Goes everywhere" means spirit exists;
translations.idiomatic: "Goes everywhere" admits spirit;

sentences.zh: 死爲休息，神無也。

translations.literal: "Death is rest" means spirit does not.
translations.idiomatic: "Death is rest" denies spirit.

sentences.zh: 原憲云：「夏后氏用明器示民無知也；

translations.literal: Yuan Xian said: "The Xia used bright vessels to show the people there was no knowing;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian said, "Xia used bright vessels to show the people had no knowing;

sentences.zh: 殷人用祭器，示人有知也；

translations.literal: the Yin used sacrificial vessels to show the people there was knowing;
translations.idiomatic: Yin used sacrificial vessels to show they had knowing;

sentences.zh: 周人兼用之，示民疑也。

translations.literal: the Zhou used both, to show the people doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou used both, to leave the people in doubt."

sentences.zh: 」考之記籍，驗之前志，有無之辯，不可歷言。

translations.literal: Examining the records and testing former chronicles, the debate over being and non-being cannot be told in full.
translations.idiomatic: Records and chronicles show the debate over being and non-being cannot be told whole.

sentences.zh: 若稽諸內教，判乎釋部，則諸子之言可尋，三代之禮無越。

translations.literal: If one weighs the inner teaching and judges within the Buddha's fold, then the words of the masters can be traced and the rites of the three dynasties do not overstep.
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the inner teaching in the Buddha's fold and the masters' words align while the three dynasties' rites stay in bounds.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 神爲生本，形爲生具。

translations.literal: Spirit is the root of life; form is life's equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit is life's root; form is its gear.

sentences.zh: 死者神離此具，而卽非彼具也。

translations.literal: The dead spirit leaves this equipment and is no longer that equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When we die the spirit leaves this gear and is no longer this gear.

sentences.zh: 雖死者不可復反，而精靈遞變，未嘗滅絕。

translations.literal: Though the dead cannot return, spirit and soul in succession change and are never extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The dead do not return, yet spirit and soul shift in turn and are never snuffed out.

sentences.zh: 當其離此之日，識用廓然，故夏后明器，示其弗反。

translations.literal: At the day they leave this body, consciousness is vast and empty; therefore the Xia's bright vessels show they do not return.
translations.idiomatic: The day they leave the body, knowing is empty—so Xia bright vessels show no return.

sentences.zh: 卽彼之時，魂靈知滅，故殷人祭器，顯其猶存。

translations.literal: At that other moment soul and spirit know extinction; therefore the Yin's sacrificial vessels show they still remain.
translations.idiomatic: Then soul and spirit know extinction—so Yin sacrificial vessels show they still remain.

sentences.zh: 不存則合乎莊周，猶存則同乎季札，各得一隅，無傷厥義。

translations.literal: If they do not remain, that agrees with Zhuang Zhou; if they remain, that agrees with Ji Zha—each holds one corner without harming the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: No remainder agrees with Zhuang Zhou; remainder with Ji Zha—each holds one corner, neither breaks the sense.

sentences.zh: 設其實也，則亦無，故周人有兼用之禮，尼父發游魂之唱，不其然乎？

translations.literal: Suppose the reality: then there is also non-being; therefore the Zhou had the rite of using both, and the Master raised the song of the wandering soul—is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Grant the reality and there is also non-being—hence Zhou's rite of both, and the Master's song of the wandering soul—is it not so?

sentences.zh: 若廢偏攜之論，探中途之旨，則不仁不智之譏，於是乎可息。

translations.literal: If one sets aside partial, one-sided doctrines and probes the middle way's intent, then the reproach of being neither benevolent nor wise may here be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Drop partial doctrines and take the middle way and the charge of lacking benevolence and wisdom can rest.

sentences.zh: 夫形也者，無知之質也；

translations.literal: Form is the substance without knowing;
translations.idiomatic: Form is substance without knowing;

sentences.zh: 神也者，有知之性也。

translations.literal: spirit is the nature with knowing.
translations.idiomatic: spirit is nature with knowing.

sentences.zh: 有知不獨存，依無知以自立，故形之於神，逆旅之館耳。

translations.literal: Knowing does not stand alone; it relies on the unknowing to set itself up—therefore form to spirit is but an inn on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing cannot stand alone; it leans on the unknowing—so form to spirit is an inn on the road.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，神去此而適彼也。

translations.literal: When death comes, spirit leaves this and goes to that.
translations.idiomatic: At death spirit leaves this and goes elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 神已去此，館何用存？

translations.literal: Spirit has already left this—of what use is the inn?
translations.idiomatic: Spirit has left—what use the inn?

sentences.zh: 速朽得理也。

translations.literal: Quick decay is according to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Quick decay is reasonable.

sentences.zh: 神已適彼，祭何所祭？

translations.literal: Spirit has already gone there—what is there to sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Spirit is already there—what is sacrifice for?

sentences.zh: 祭則失理。

translations.literal: To sacrifice is to miss reason.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice misses reason.

sentences.zh: 而姬、孔之教不然者，其有以乎！

translations.literal: Yet the teaching of Ji and Kong is not so—must there be a cause!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ji and Kong taught otherwise—there must be a reason!

sentences.zh: 蓋禮樂之興，出於澆薄，俎豆綴兆，生於俗弊。

translations.literal: Rites and music arose from a thinning age; offering stands and grave mounds sprang from vulgar decay.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music rose from a thin age; offering stands and grave mounds from vulgar rot.

sentences.zh: 施靈筵，陳棺槨，設饋奠，建丘隴，蓋欲令孝子有追思之地耳，夫何補於已遷之神乎？

translations.literal: Setting spirit altars, arraying coffins, laying out funeral feasts, building mound and ridge—all was to give the filial son a place for longing; what does it mend the spirit already gone?
translations.idiomatic: Spirit altars, coffins, funeral feasts, mounds and ridges—all so the filial son might mourn; what help to a spirit already gone?

sentences.zh: 故上古衣之以薪，棄之中野，可謂尊盧、赫胥、皇雄、炎帝蹈於失理哉？

translations.literal: Therefore in high antiquity they clothed the dead in firewood and cast them in the wild—can we say Chonglu, Hexu, Huangxiong, and Yandi trampled on reason?
translations.idiomatic: High antiquity wrapped the dead in firewood and cast them in the wild—were Chonglu, Hexu, Huangxiong, and Yandi wrong?

sentences.zh: 是以子羽沉川，漢伯方壙，文楚黃壤，士安麻索。

translations.literal: Thus Ziyu sank in the river, Han Bo in a great mound, King Wen in yellow earth, and Shi An in hemp rope.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu sank in the river, Han Bo in a great mound, King Wen in yellow earth, Shi An in hemp rope.

sentences.zh: 此四子者，得理也，忘教也。

translations.literal: These four men grasped reason and forgot the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: These four grasped reason and forgot the teaching.

sentences.zh: 若從四子而游，則平生之志得矣。

translations.literal: If one followed the four men in roaming, one's lifelong aim would be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the four and a lifetime's aim would be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 然積習生常，難卒改革，一朝肆志，儻不見從。

translations.literal: Yet accumulated habit becomes custom and is hard to reform at once; to give free rein to one's will in a single morning—perhaps none would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Habit becomes custom and is hard to break overnight; to act at once on one's will—perhaps none would follow.

sentences.zh: 今欲剪截煩厚，務存儉易；

translations.literal: Now I wish to cut away the cumbersome and thick and strive to keep what is spare and easy;
translations.idiomatic: Now I would cut the cumbersome and keep what is spare and easy;

sentences.zh: 進不裸尸，退異常俗；

translations.literal: advance not to bare the corpse, retreat yet differ from common custom;
translations.idiomatic: not bare the corpse, yet differ from common custom;

sentences.zh: 不傷存者之念，有合至人之道。

translations.literal: not harming the living in their thoughts, yet agreeing with the Way of the perfected man.
translations.idiomatic: not wounding the living, yet matching the perfected man's Way.

sentences.zh: 孔子云：「斂首足形，還葬而無槨。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Wrap head and feet and shape, return to burial without inner coffin."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Wrap head and feet and shape, bury without inner coffin."

sentences.zh: 」斯亦貧者之禮也，余何陋焉？

translations.literal: That too is the rite of the poor—what is base in me?
translations.idiomatic: That is the poor man's rite—what is base in me?

sentences.zh: 且張奐止用幅巾，王肅唯盥手足，范冉殮畢便葬，奚珍無設筵幾，文度故舟爲槨，子廉牛車載柩，叔起誡絕墳隴，康成使無卜吉。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhang Huan used only a headcloth, Wang Su washed only hands and feet, Fan Ran was buried as soon as wrapping was done, Xi Zhen set no altar or table, Wen Du once made his boat the coffin, Zilian carried the bier on an ox cart, Shuji warned against grave mounds, and Kang Cheng had no divination for auspicious ground.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan used only a headcloth, Wang Su washed only hands and feet, Fan Ran buried at once, Xi Zhen set no altar, Wen Du made his boat the coffin, Zilian used an ox cart, Shuji warned against mounds, Kang Cheng forwent divination.

sentences.zh: 此數公者，尚或如之；

translations.literal: These gentlemen at least did so;
translations.idiomatic: These men at least did so;

sentences.zh: 況於吾人，而當華泰！

translations.literal: how much more for a man like me should there be pomp and splendor!
translations.idiomatic: how much more should I parade pomp and splendor!

sentences.zh: 今欲仿佛景行，以爲軌則，儻合中庸之道，庶免徒費之譏。

translations.literal: Now I wish to take their bright conduct as measure and rule, and if it fits the middle way perhaps I may escape the reproach of waste in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Now I take their bright conduct as measure; if it fits the middle way I may escape vain waste.

sentences.zh: 氣絕不須復魂，盥洗而斂。

translations.literal: When breath fails there is no need to recall the soul; wash and wrap.
translations.idiomatic: When breath fails, do not recall the soul—wash and wrap.

sentences.zh: 以一千錢市治棺、單故裙衫、衣巾枕履。

translations.literal: With one thousand cash buy a plain coffin, old skirt and jacket, clothes, towel, pillow, and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Spend a thousand cash on a plain coffin, old skirt and jacket, clothes, towel, pillow, and shoes.

sentences.zh: 此外送往之具，棺中常物，及餘閣之祭，一不得有所施。

translations.literal: Beyond that, whatever is sent off with the bier, ordinary things in the coffin, and remaining side offerings—nothing may be laid out.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, whatever goes with the bier, ordinary coffin goods, and side offerings—nothing may be laid out.

sentences.zh: 世多信李、彭之言，可謂惑矣。

translations.literal: The age mostly believes the words of Li and Peng—one may call that delusion.
translations.idiomatic: The age mostly believes Li and Peng—call that delusion.

sentences.zh: 余以孔、釋爲師，差無此惑。

translations.literal: I take Kong and the Buddha as teachers and am somewhat free of this delusion.
translations.idiomatic: I take Confucius and the Buddha as teachers and am somewhat free of this delusion.

sentences.zh: 斂訖，載以露車，歸於舊山，隨得一地，地足爲坎，坎足容棺，不須磚甓，不勞封樹，勿設祭饗，勿置几筵，無用茅君之虛座，伯夷之杅水。

translations.literal: When wrapping is done, load on an open cart and return to the old hill; wherever ground suffices for a pit and the pit suffices for the coffin—no bricks, no labor to mound and plant trees, no funeral feast, no altar table, no empty seat of Lord Mao, no Yi Bo's libation water.
translations.idiomatic: When wrapping is done, load on an open cart to the old hill; wherever a pit fits the coffin—no brick, no mound, no funeral feast, no altar, no Lord Mao's empty seat, no Yi Bo's libation water.

sentences.zh: 其蒸嘗繼嗣，言象所絕，事止余身，無傷世教。

translations.literal: As for seasonal offerings and heirs, what image and speech cut off—let the matter stop with my body without harming the world's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal offerings and heirs—what image and speech cut off—let it stop with my body and not harm the world's teaching.

sentences.zh: 家人長幼，內外姻戚，凡厥友朋，爰及寓所，咸願成余之志，幸勿奪之。

translations.literal: Family young and old, kin within and without, all friends, and every lodging I have known—each alike wishes to fulfill my will; pray do not wrest it away.
translations.idiomatic: Family, kin, friends, and every lodging I have known—all wish to fulfill my will; pray do not wrest it away.

sentences.zh: 明年疾卒，時年三十二。

translations.literal: The next year he died of illness, aged thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died of illness, at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 歊幼時嘗獨坐空室，有一老公至門，謂歊曰：「心力勇猛，能精死生；

translations.literal: When Shao was young he once sat alone in an empty room; an old man came to the door and said to Shao: "Mind and strength are fierce; you can penetrate death and life—
translations.idiomatic: Young, Shao sat alone in an empty room; an old man at the door said, "Mind and strength are fierce; you can penetrate death and life—

sentences.zh: 但不得久滯一方耳。

translations.literal: only you cannot long linger in one place."
translations.idiomatic: only you cannot long linger in one place."

sentences.zh: 」因彈指而去。

translations.literal: He snapped his fingers and left.
translations.idiomatic: He snapped his fingers and left.

sentences.zh: 歊旣長，精心學佛。

translations.literal: When Shao had grown he devoted his mind to learning Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he devoted his mind to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 有道人釋寶志者，時人莫測也，遇歊於興皇寺，驚起曰：「隱居學道，清淨登佛。

translations.literal: There was a monk, Shibao Zhi, whom men of the time could not fathom; meeting Shao at Xinghuang Monastery he started up and said: "Reclusion and the Way, purity and ascent to Buddhahood."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Shibao Zhi, whom no one could fathom, met Shao at Xinghuang Monastery and cried: "Reclusion and the Way, purity and Buddhahood."

sentences.zh: 」如此三說。

translations.literal: " Thus he spoke three times.
translations.idiomatic: " He said this three times.

sentences.zh: 歊未死之春，有人爲其庭中栽柿，歊謂兄子弇曰：「吾不見此實，爾其勿言。

translations.literal: In the spring before Xiao died, someone planted a persimmon in his courtyard; Xiao told his nephew Yan, "I shall not see this fruit—do not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The spring before Xiao died someone planted a persimmon in his yard; he told his nephew Yan, "I will not live to see this fruit—say nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 」至秋而亡，人以爲知命。

translations.literal: " When autumn came he died; men thought him prescient about fate.
translations.idiomatic: " He died that autumn; people took it as knowledge of fate.

sentences.zh: 親故誄其行跡，諡曰貞節處士。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends eulogized his conduct and posthumously titled him Recluse of Chaste Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends eulogized his life and gave him the posthumous title Recluse of Chaste Integrity.

sentences.zh: 庾詵字彥寶，新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Shen, styled Yanshi, was a man of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shen, styled Yanshi, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 幼聰警篤學，經史百家無不該綜，緯候書射，棊釐機巧，並一時之絕。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever and devoted to learning; classics, history, and the hundred schools he mastered entirely—weft-texts, divination, writing, archery, go, and mechanical ingenuity were all unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and studious from youth, he mastered classics, history, and every school—weft-texts, divination, writing, archery, go, and ingenious craft were unrivaled in his day.

sentences.zh: 而性託夷簡，特愛林泉。

translations.literal: Yet his nature inclined to plain simplicity; he especially loved forests and springs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was plain and simple by nature and loved woods and streams above all.

sentences.zh: 十畝之宅，山池居半。

translations.literal: In a ten-mu dwelling, hills and ponds occupied half.
translations.idiomatic: Half his ten-mu home was hill and pond.

sentences.zh: 蔬食弊衣，不治產業。

translations.literal: He ate vegetables and wore worn clothes and did not manage property.
translations.idiomatic: He ate plain food, wore threadbare clothes, and kept no estate.

sentences.zh: 嘗乘舟從田舍還，載米一百五十石，有人寄載三十石。

translations.literal: Once returning by boat from his fields he carried a hundred fifty piculs of rice; someone asked to load thirty piculs aboard.
translations.idiomatic: Once boating back from his fields with a hundred fifty piculs of rice, a man asked to ship thirty piculs with him.

sentences.zh: 旣至宅，寄載者曰：「君三十斛，我百五十石。

translations.literal: When he reached home the loader said, "You have thirty hu, I have a hundred fifty piculs.
translations.idiomatic: At home the loader said, "You have thirty hu; I have a hundred fifty piculs.

sentences.zh: 」詵默然不言，恣其取足。

translations.literal: " Shen kept silent and let him take all he wanted.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen said nothing and let him take what he would.

sentences.zh: 鄰人有被誣爲盜者，被治劾，妄款，詵矜之，乃以書質錢二萬，令門生詐爲其親，代之酬備。

translations.literal: A neighbor falsely accused as a thief was prosecuted and confessed under duress; Shen took pity, pawned books for twenty thousand cash, and had a disciple pose as kin to pay compensation in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor wrongly charged as a thief was beaten into confession; Shen pitied him, pawned books for twenty thousand cash, and had a student pose as kin to pay the damages.

sentences.zh: 鄰人獲免，謝詵，詵曰：「吾矜天下無辜，豈期謝也。

translations.literal: The neighbor was freed and thanked Shen; Shen said, "I pity all the innocent under heaven—why would I expect thanks?
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor was cleared and thanked him; Shen said, "I pity the innocent everywhere—why expect thanks?

sentences.zh: 」其行多如此類。

translations.literal: " His conduct was mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: " Most of his deeds were like this.

sentences.zh: 高祖少與詵善，雅推重之。

translations.literal: Gaozu in youth was friendly with Shen and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu knew Shen from youth and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及起義，署爲平西府記室參軍，詵不屈。

translations.literal: When the uprising began he appointed him Army staff officer of the Pacify-the-West headquarters; Shen would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: At the uprising he made Shen staff officer of the Pacify-the-West headquarters; Shen refused.

sentences.zh: 平生少所遊狎，河東柳惲欲與之交，詵距而不納。

translations.literal: All his life he kept few intimates; Liu Yun of Hedong wished to befriend him, but Shen refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He kept few close friends; Liu Yun of Hedong sought his friendship, but Shen turned him away.

sentences.zh: 後湘東王臨荊州，板爲鎮西府記室參軍，不就。

translations.literal: Later when Prince Xiangdong governed Jingzhou, he was appointed Army staff officer of the Pacify-the-West headquarters; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Xiangdong at Jingzhou made him Pacify-the-West staff officer; he declined.

sentences.zh: 普通中，詔曰：「明敭振滯，爲政所先；

translations.literal: In the Putong era an edict said, "Brightly raise the stalled—this is foremost in government;
translations.idiomatic: Putong era edict: "To raise the stalled is government's first duty;

sentences.zh: 旌賢求士，夢佇斯急。

translations.literal: to honor the worthy and seek scholars—this is what one dreams of in urgency.
translations.idiomatic: to honor talent and seek scholars is the urgent dream of rule.

sentences.zh: 新野庾詵，止足棲退，自事卻掃，經史文藝，多所貫習；

translations.literal: Yu Shen of Xinye, content to stop and dwell in withdrawal, busies himself sweeping his threshold; classics, history, and letters he has largely mastered;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shen of Xinye, knowing when to stop and live apart, keeps his own threshold; he is deeply versed in classics, history, and letters;

sentences.zh: 潁川庾承先，學通黃、老，該涉釋教；

translations.literal: Yu Chengxian of Yingchuan, learned in Yellow Emperor and Laozi, also versed in Buddhist teaching;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chengxian of Yingchuan masters Huang-Lao learning and knows Buddhist teaching;

sentences.zh: 並不競不營，安茲枯槁，可以鎮躁敦俗。

translations.literal: both unambitious and unenterprising, settled in this withered state—they can steady rashness and thicken custom.
translations.idiomatic: both unambitious and unworldly, content in austerity—they can calm hot tempers and thicken custom.

sentences.zh: 詵可黃門侍郎，承先可中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Shen may be Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, Chengxian may be Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shen is appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates; Chengxian, Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 勒州縣時加敦遣，庶能屈志，方冀鹽梅。

translations.literal: Let provinces and commanderies press them with timely urging, hoping they may bend their will—we look to them as salt and sour plum.
translations.idiomatic: Let provinces and districts urge them in season, hoping to win their assent—we count on them as salt and plum.

sentences.zh: 」詵稱疾不赴。

translations.literal: " Shen pleaded illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: " Shen pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 晚年以後，尤遵釋教。

translations.literal: In his later years he especially followed Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he devoted himself still more to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 宅內立道場，環繞禮懺，六時不輟。

translations.literal: Within his house he established a dharma hall, circumambulating and performing repentance, six periods without pause.
translations.idiomatic: He built a dharma hall at home and ceaselessly circled it in repentance, six times daily without rest.

sentences.zh: 誦《法華經》，每日一遍。

translations.literal: He chanted the *Lotus Sutra* once each day.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he chanted the *Lotus Sutra* once through.

sentences.zh: 後夜中忽見一道人，自稱願公，容止甚異，呼詵爲上行先生，授香而去。

translations.literal: Later one night he suddenly saw a Daoist priest who called himself Master Yuan, very strange in bearing, who addressed Shen as "Master of the Higher Path," gave incense, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: One night he saw a priest calling himself Master Yuan, oddly composed, who hailed Shen as Master of the Higher Path, gave incense, and left.

sentences.zh: 中大通四年，因晝寢，忽驚覺曰：「願公復來，不可久住。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongdatong, waking from a daytime nap, he started and said, "Master Yuan comes again—I cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdatong year four, waking from a nap, he started and said, "Master Yuan returns—I cannot linger.

sentences.zh: 」顏色不變，言終而卒，時年七十八。

translations.literal: " His countenance unchanged, at the end of his words he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: " His face unchanged, he died as he finished speaking, at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 舉室咸聞空中唱「上行先生已生彌陁淨域矣」。

translations.literal: The whole household heard a voice in the air chant, "The Master of the Higher Path has been born in Amitabha's Pure Land."
translations.idiomatic: All in the house heard a voice from the sky: "Master of the Higher Path is born in Amitabha's Pure Land."

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而下詔曰：「旌善表行，前王所敦。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard and issued an edict: "Honoring good and displaying conduct—former kings made this their instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard and decreed: "To honor virtue and show conduct is what former kings enjoined.

sentences.zh: 新野庾詵，荊山珠玉，江陵杞梓，靜侯南度，固有名德，獨貞苦節，孤芳素履。

translations.literal: Yu Shen of Xinye—pearl and jade of Jingshan, catalpa and paulownia of Jiangling; when the quiet marquis crossed south he had fame and virtue; alone in bitter integrity and solitary pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shen of Xinye—Jingshan pearl, Jiangling timber; when the quiet marquis fled south his name and virtue were sure; alone in harsh integrity and pure solitary walk.

sentences.zh: 奄隨運往，惻愴於懷。

translations.literal: Suddenly gone with fate's turn, grief fills the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly taken by fate, the heart is sore with grief.

sentences.zh: 宜諡貞節處士，以顯高烈。

translations.literal: He should be posthumously titled Recluse of Chaste Integrity to display his lofty virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be titled Recluse of Chaste Integrity, that his high virtue may shine.

sentences.zh: 」詵所撰《帝曆》二十卷、《易林》二十卷、續伍端休《江陵記》一卷、《晉朝雜事》五卷、《總抄》八十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: " Shen wrote *Imperial Calendars* in twenty scrolls, *Forest of Changes* in twenty, continued Wu Duanxiu's *Record of Jiangling* in one, *Miscellaneous Affairs of Jin* in five, and *General Collection* in eighty—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " His works included twenty scrolls each of *Imperial Calendars* and *Forest of Changes*, one scroll continuing Wu Duanxiu's *Record of Jiangling*, five of *Miscellaneous Affairs of Jin*, and eighty of *General Collection*—all in circulation.

sentences.zh: 子曼倩字世華，亦早有令譽。

translations.literal: His son Manqian, styled Shihua, also early won fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Manqian, styled Shihua, won early fame as well.

sentences.zh: 世祖在荊州，辟爲主簿，遷中錄事。

translations.literal: When Shizu was in Jingzhou he recruited him as chief clerk, then promoted him to central recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu at Jingzhou made him chief clerk, then central recorder.

sentences.zh: 每出，世祖常目送之，謂劉之遴曰：「荊南信多君子，雖美歸田鳳，清屬桓階，賞德標奇，未過此子。

translations.literal: Each time he went out Shizu would watch him go and say to Liu Zhilin, "Jingnan truly has many gentlemen—though Gui Tianfeng is beautiful and Huan Jie is pure, in praising virtue and marking excellence none surpasses this boy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Manqian left, Shizu watched him go and told Liu Zhilin, "Jingnan has true gentlemen—Gui Tianfeng is fair and Huan Jie is clear, but for honoring virtue none outdoes this lad.

sentences.zh: 」後轉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: " Later he became advisory staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he became advisory staff officer.

sentences.zh: 所著《喪服儀》、《文字體例》、《莊老義疏》，注《算經》及《七曜歷術》，幷所制文章，凡九十五卷。

translations.literal: His works include *Mourning Garb Rites*, *Character Forms and Rules*, and *Exegesis on Zhuangzi and Laozi*, commentaries on the *Classic of Computation* and *Seven Luminaries Calendar Methods*, together with his own compositions—ninety-five scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote *Mourning Garb Rites*, *Character Forms and Rules*, *Exegesis on Zhuangzi and Laozi*, commentaries on the *Classic of Computation* and *Seven Luminaries Calendar Methods*, and his own essays—ninety-five scrolls all told.

sentences.zh: 子季才，有學行。

translations.literal: His son Jicai had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jicai had scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 承聖中，仕至中書侍郎。

translations.literal: During Chengsheng he served up to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengsheng he rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷，隨例入關。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell he entered the pass with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he went into the north with the others.

sentences.zh: 張孝秀

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiu

sentences.zh: 張孝秀字文逸，南陽宛人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoxiu, styled Wenyi, was a man of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoxiu, styled Wenyi, came from Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 少仕州爲治中從事史。

translations.literal: In youth he served the province as aide to the inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was provincial aide to the inspector.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，服闋，爲建安王別駕。

translations.literal: After mourning his mother, when mourning ended he became vice-administrator to the Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning he became vice-administrator to the Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遂去職歸山，居于東林寺。

translations.literal: Soon after he resigned and returned to the mountains, dwelling at East Grove Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he quit office for the hills and lived at East Grove Temple.

sentences.zh: 有田數十頃，部曲數百人，率以力田，盡供山衆，遠近歸慕，赴之如市。

translations.literal: He had several dozen qing of fields and several hundred retainers, all farming—supplying the mountain community entirely; men near and far admired him and came as to a market.
translations.idiomatic: He held dozens of qing and hundreds of retainers who farmed for the monastery; admirers near and far flocked to him like a market.

sentences.zh: 孝秀性通率，不好浮華，常冠穀皮巾，躡蒲履，手執幷櫚皮麈尾。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiu was open and straightforward by nature, disliking ornament; he often wore a grain-husk headcloth, straw sandals, and in hand a combined palm-bark flywhisk.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and unpretentious, he usually wore a grain-husk cap, straw shoes, and carried a palm-bark flywhisk.

sentences.zh: 服寒食散，盛冬能臥於石。

translations.literal: He took cold-food powder and in deep winter could lie on stone.
translations.idiomatic: He used cold-food powder and in deep winter could sleep on bare stone.

sentences.zh: 博涉羣書，專精釋典。

translations.literal: He ranged widely in books and specialized in Buddhist canon.
translations.idiomatic: He read broadly and mastered Buddhist scripture.

sentences.zh: 善談論，工隸書，凡諸藝能，莫不明習。

translations.literal: He was skilled at debate and clerical script; of every art none was unknown to him.
translations.idiomatic: He debated well, wrote clerical script expertly, and knew every craft worth knowing.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，卒，時年四十二，室中皆聞有非常香氣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong he died, aged forty-two; throughout the room an extraordinary fragrance was sensed.
translations.idiomatic: Putong year three he died at forty-two; a strange fragrance filled the room.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞，甚傷悼焉，與劉慧斐書，述其貞白雲。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and grieved deeply; he wrote to Liu Huifei describing his pure white conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him and wrote Liu Huifei praising his pure life.

sentences.zh: 庾承先

translations.literal: Yu Chengxian
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chengxian

sentences.zh: 庾承先字子通，潁川𨻳陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chengxian, styled Zitong, was a man of Dingling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chengxian, styled Zitong, came from Dingling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 少沉靜有志操，是非不涉於言，喜慍不形於色，人莫能窺也。

translations.literal: From youth he was quiet and possessed firm resolve; right and wrong did not enter his speech, joy and anger did not show on his face—none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and principled from youth, he never spoke of right and wrong and never showed joy or anger—no one could read him.

sentences.zh: 弱歲受學於南陽劉虯，強記敏識，出於羣輩。

translations.literal: In early youth he studied under Liu Ou of Nanyang; strong in memory and quick in perception, he stood above his peers.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he studied with Liu Ou of Nanyang; his memory and wit surpassed his fellows.

sentences.zh: 玄經釋典，靡不該悉；

translations.literal: Dark learning and Buddhist canon—none he did not comprehend;
translations.idiomatic: Dark learning and Buddhist scripture—he knew them all;

sentences.zh: 九流《七略》，咸所精練。

translations.literal: The Nine Currents and the *Seven Summaries*—all he mastered.
translations.idiomatic: the Nine Currents and the *Seven Summaries*—all he had mastered.

sentences.zh: 郡辟功曹不就，乃與道士王僧鎮同游衡岳。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as merit officer; he did not go, and instead traveled Mt Heng with Daoist Wang Sengzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as commandery merit officer, he refused and roamed Mt Heng with the Daoist Wang Sengzhen.

sentences.zh: 晚以弟疾還鄉里，遂居于土臺山。

translations.literal: Late in life, because his brother was ill he returned home and settled on Mt Tutai.
translations.idiomatic: Later, his brother fell ill; he went home and settled on Mt Tutai.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽忠烈王在州，欽其風味，要與遊處。

translations.literal: Prince Zhonglie of Poyang while governing the province admired his flavor and invited him to keep company.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhonglie of Poyang, governing the province, prized his character and asked his company.

sentences.zh: 又令講《老子》，遠近名僧，咸來赴集，論難鋒起，異端競至，承先徐相酬答，皆得所未聞。

translations.literal: He also had him lecture on the *Laozi*; eminent monks near and far all came; sharp debate arose and heterodoxies competed; Chengxian slowly answered each, all hearing what they had never heard.
translations.idiomatic: He had him expound the *Laozi*; famous monks gathered from afar; debate flared and odd doctrines piled in—Chengxian answered calmly, and all heard things new to them.

sentences.zh: 忠烈王尤加欽重，徵州主簿；

translations.literal: Prince Zhonglie especially honored him and summoned him as provincial chief clerk;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhonglie honored him still more and summoned him as provincial chief clerk;

sentences.zh: 湘東王聞之，亦板爲法曹參軍；

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong heard and also appointed him legal bureau staff officer;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong heard and also made him legal bureau staff officer;

sentences.zh: 並不赴。

translations.literal: he went to neither.
translations.idiomatic: he accepted neither post.

sentences.zh: 中大通三年，廬山劉慧斐至荊州，承先與之有舊，往從之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongdatong Liu Huifei of Lushan came to Jingzhou; Chengxian had old ties with him and went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdatong year three Liu Huifei of Lushan reached Jingzhou; Chengxian, an old friend, went to him.

sentences.zh: 荊陝學徒，因請承先講《老子》。

translations.literal: Students of Jing and Shan then asked Chengxian to lecture on the *Laozi*.
translations.idiomatic: Students of Jing and Shan asked Chengxian to lecture on the *Laozi*.

sentences.zh: 湘東王親命駕臨聽，論議終日，深相賞接。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangdong personally ordered his carriage to listen; debate lasted all day and he deeply appreciated and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiangdong drove out to hear him; they debated all day and the prince greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 留連月餘日，乃還山。

translations.literal: After lingering more than a month he returned to the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed over a month, then went back to the hills.

sentences.zh: 王親祖道，幷贈篇什，隱者美之。

translations.literal: The prince personally saw him off and also bestowed verse; recluses praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince saw him off in person and gave him poems; recluses admired them.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died, at sixty.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：世之誣處士者，多云純盜虛名，而無適用，蓋有負其實者。

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, said: Those who malign recluses often say they merely steal empty fame without practical use—yet there are those who fail to put their substance to use.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen Minister of Personnel, said: Men who slander recluses call them empty fame with no use—but some gifted men simply never deploy their gifts.

sentences.zh: 若諸葛璩之學術，阮孝緒之簿閥，其取進也豈難哉？

translations.literal: If men like Zhuge Ju's scholarship and Ruan Xiaoxiu's genealogical mastery—would advancing have been difficult for them?
translations.idiomatic: For men like Zhuge Ju in learning and Ruan Xiaoxiu in genealogy—was high office ever hard to win?

sentences.zh: 終於隱居，固亦性而已矣。

translations.literal: Yet they ended in reclusion—after all, that was simply their nature.
translations.idiomatic: They ended in withdrawal—it was only their nature.
